## [v2]

reason: The claim's premise is half-right and its conclusion is wrong for omp. "omp has refresh tokens" is true and badly understated. "modifyRecord as the only write path" is real in dsh — but omp ALREADY SHIPS A STRICTLY BETTER VERSION, so the port is not net-positive; it is a regression.

REFUTATION 1 — omp already has a superior mechanism, measured. omp has a durable cross-process lease + fenced compare-and-swap: a real `auth_credential_refresh_leases` SQLite table (sqlite-credential-store.ts:540-546), `tryAcquireCredentialRefreshLease` with steal-on-expiry in the ON CONFLICT WHERE clause (:480-487), `renewCredentialRefreshLease` (:492-493), `releaseCredentialRefreshLease` (:495-496), and `tryUpdateAuthCredentialIfMatches(id, expectedData, credential, lease)` (:1438-1477). TTL 15s, renew every 5s, poll 50ms (refresh.ts:33-35). The full protocol is refresh.ts:83-293.

REFUTATION 2 — the designs differ on the one point that matters under load. dsh's `modifyRecord` holds a `withFileLock` across `await mutate(current)` (credentials-local/src/index.ts:676-682) — and mutate does the token-refresh network round trip. dsh's own code admits this: "a credential mutation that refreshes a token performs a network round trip while holding the lock" (util/atomic-write/src/index.ts:201-208), which is why `waitMs` exists at all. omp's lease is RENEWED IN A BACKGROUND LOOP while the HTTP refresh is in flight (refresh.ts:176-194), so no lock is held across the network. omp spawns workers, runs a local auth-broker, and shares one credentials DB across processes; swapping a renewable lease for a lock-held-across-network would be strictly worse there.

REFUTATION 3 — the one-write-path rule would destroy working semantics. omp's `CredentialRowStore` (store.ts:52-84) has 7 write methods that are NOT interchangeable `modifyRecord`s: `updateAuthCredential`, `tryDisableAuthCredentialIfMatches`, `tryUpdateAuthCredentialIfMatches`, `replaceAuthCredentials`, `upsertAuthCredential`, `deleteAuthCredential`, `deleteAuthCredentials`. They differ in fence semantics (CAS-on-expectedData, lease-fenced, bulk-replace) and in the broker-delegation contract — `upsertAuthCredential`/`replaceAuthCredentials` are async, must forward to the broker AND update the local snapshot before returning (store.ts:78-82; auth-broker/remote-store.ts:878, 891). A single sync `modifyRecord(key, mutate)` shape cannot express "forward to remote broker then mutate local snapshot". This is defended by 20 race tests in auth-storage-oauth-refresh-race.test.ts (998 LOC), including "does not overwrite a peer rotation after releasing the refresh lease" (:452) and two lease-loss-before-CAS tests (:762, :816).

REFUTATION 4 — the named port target has no host. grep for credential|oauth|auth|token across packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/ returns only git path tokenization (custom-commands/bundled/review/diff.ts) and `maxTokens` (text-summary.ts:29). `grep -rn modifyRecord packages/` in omp = 0 hits.

REFUTATION 5 — the one extensibility credential surface is a deliberate non-write. extensions/types.ts:1631-1643 exposes `refreshToken?(credentials): Promise<OAuthCredentials>` — a PURE TRANSFORM with no write capability; omp's OAuthRefresher persists the result. Porting dsh's shape would put third-party plugin code inside the credential store's read-decide-replace callback, handing arbitrary extension authors write authority over the credential store and a cross-process lock across their network call. Security + deadlock regression.

TIERS — DO-NOT-COPY: the one-write-path rule itself. BORROW (docs-only, zero-risk): dsh's interface-comment discipline stating WHY a write path is serialized (credentials/src/index.ts:163-168, 236-242). omp's store.ts:52-84 documents what each method does but the rationale lives in refresh.ts implementation comments, not the contract — moving it to the interface is cheap. REFERENCE: the `waitMs` rationale (atomic-write/src/index.ts:198-209) as a design note.

CITATION ERROR: the claim cites credentials/src/index.ts:256-262 for the token-refresh justification. Lines 256-262 are `deleteRecord` (:256) and the `notifyUpdated` doc block (:258-267). The actual "the only write path" + "a token refresh is read-decide-replace under one lock" text is at :236-250 (method doc) and :163-168 (class doc). Substance verified; line range wrong.

(1) WRONG FILE FOR 2 OF 3 TYPES. The claim places all three at `credentials/src/types.ts:65-68`. Reality: only `CredentialInfo` is in types.ts, at lines 67-74. `CredentialRecordInfo` is at `packages/credentials/credentials/src/index.ts:126-138` and `CredentialRecordEntry` at `index.ts:141-146`. This is not pedantry — it inverts the point. types.ts:1-9 declares its purpose as the *client-safe* surface: "Types only — no runtime code, and nothing here reaches a Host-only symbol, so a Client compilation face reads exactly the signature the Host emits." index.ts is the Host service module (it imports `@deepseek-ai/cordis`, line 11). The two record types are on the Host side BY CONSTRUCTION — they are not client-safe-face types at all.

(2) "THE ENTIRE READ HALF CROSSES A WIRE" IS FALSE — 2 OF 3 NEVER CROSS. The wire carries exactly one credential method. `packages/api/settings-controller/src/credentials.ts` exposes exactly 3 `@Remote` methods (lines 82, 99, 112): `describe`, `set`, `unset`. The repo's own test pins this: `remoteMethods(controller)` must equal exactly those three (tests/credentials-controller.host.spec.ts:47-51). `describe` returns `Record<string, CredentialInfo>`. `describeRecord` and `listRecords` — the methods backed by the other two types — are never Remote-exposed: zero hits across `packages/api`, `packages/client`, `packages/remotes`. The only client-face export is `CredentialInfo` ALONE (packages/api/remotes/src/client/index.ts:136, "values never ride it"). So the claim's read half is one method, not three types.

(3) THE TYPE IS NOT WHAT MAKES IT SAFE — A RUNTIME PROJECTION IS. Causation is inverted. Enforcement is `projectCredentialInfo` (credentials.ts:45-51), a field-by-field copy, needed because the type does NOT stop a secret riding. `CredentialInfo.source?: string` (types.ts:71) is an unconstrained provider-defined string, copied verbatim by the projection. The repo's own test proves a foreign provider can smuggle a value past the type: `LeakyCredentials.describe()` returns `{ configured: true, source: 'memory', writable: true, value: 'sk-leaked' } as CredentialInfo` (test:12) — the `as` assertion suppresses excess-property checking, so TypeScript accepts the extra `value`. The test at :101-106 ("answers only the fields the view declares, whatever a provider returns") exists PRECISELY BECAUSE the type is not the guarantee. The value-free interface is the declared contract; the projection is the enforcement. The claim credits the shape with the property the function delivers.

(4) THE NORMATIVE HALF IS WRONG ABOUT dsh AND MOOT FOR omp. dsh's actual settings view does NOT use these types. `SettingsNamespaceView` (packages/settings/settings/src/types.ts:22-38) uses its own `SettingsSecretView { path: string[]; set: boolean }` plus a `redactSecrets` mechanism (packages/settings/settings/src/index.ts:323-330). Its comment (types.ts:19-21) is a STRONGER discipline than CredentialInfo's: the JSON fields are `JsonValue` not `unknown` "because the Remote boundary admits no unconstrained data" — that forbids unconstrained data outright, where `source?: string` is a free-form string a secret rides in with zero type objection. So "settings view needs this shape" is misdirected: dsh's settings namespace has its own vocabulary, and the credential types serve the credentials namespace.

For omp: no such surface exists. Zero hits for `CredentialInfo`/`CredentialRecordInfo`/`CredentialRecordEntry` AND zero for `CredentialProvider`/`credentialRef`/`credentialKey` — omp has no credential seam, so there is nothing to shape. Per hard rule 3 I did not treat the 0 hits as proof: omp's remote surface under another name is `packages/senpi-desktop-protocol` (775 LOC total incl. tests), and it is a computer-use JSON-RPC — click, type, screenshot, clipboard, window (method allowlist at test/method-allowlist.test.ts:4-38), not a settings/credential protocol. `packages/web` is a marketing/docs Next.js site. omp's MCP credential handling is `packages/mcp-client-core/src/mcp-oauth/storage.ts:16-23`, a local file store with a loopback callback server — no remote settings view.

TIERS — BORROW: the field-by-field projection plus the exact-method-allowlist assertion is the genuinely transferable pattern, and it is a runtime function, not the "value-free type" the claim credits. Also `redactSecrets` (schema-driven redaction + a parallel slot list) is the stronger idea for a real settings surface. REFERENCE: the credential seam's two-key-space split (ref = env-var name, key = `<scope>/<id>`) and its empty-value-is-absent rule. DO-NOT-COPY: crediting a TS interface with a wire-safety property it does not enforce; and treating an `as`-asserted provider return as type-checked.

reason: REFUTED on three independent grounds, all measured by reading both codebases.

(1) THE MECHANISM IS MISATTRIBUTED — dsh's own code proves the type is insufficient. The claim says the value-free type is what makes "the entire read half safe to cross a wire." dsh ships the opposite lesson. `packages/api/settings-controller/src/credentials.ts:45-51` defines `projectCredentialInfo()`, and its JSDoc at :39-41 states why: "The Gateway returns a business result without decoding it, so a provider whose `describe` carried extra enumerable properties would otherwise serialize them to the caller." TypeScript structural typing does NOT strip extra properties, so the declared shape is insufficient and an explicit field-by-field copy is load-bearing. dsh's own test proves the hole: `credentials-controller.host.spec.ts:9-15` defines `LeakyCredentials` whose `describe()` returns `{ configured: true, source: 'memory', writable: true, value: 'sk-leaked' } as CredentialInfo` — a secret riding in a field the type never declares, admitted by a one-token cast. The test at :101-106 pins the projection as the thing that strips it. The claim ships the half that does not work and omits the half that does.

(2) THE CITATION IS WRONG FOR 2 OF 3 TYPES. `CredentialInfo` is at `credentials/src/types.ts:67-74` (claim's ":65-68" lands on the JSDoc tail + interface head — loose but roughly right). (3) THE TARGET SURFACE DOES NOT EXIST IN omp. In ACP, the only `settings` field that crosses is a model-ID table (`acp-agent.ts:257`); the other hits pass the internal `record.session.settings` object to builtin slash commands, not to the client. There is nothing to port the type FOR.

DO-NOT-COPY / already-better in omp, both strictly stronger:

## [v2]

reason: REFUTED on portability, on four independent grounds. The code claim is accurate but the source attribution is wrong, and the pattern is a net-negative port.

SOURCE MIS-ATTRIBUTION: "dsh/safety-sandbox-guard" does not exist. `grep -rln "safety-sandbox-guard" --include=package.json` over deepseek-harness returns zero hits; there is no such directory. The code lives in the *credentials* package, not a safety sandbox.

WHAT IS TRUE: `assertOwnerOnly` is real at dsh `packages/credentials/credentials-local/src/index.ts:127-146` — stats, returns early on win32 (:137), tests `mode & 0o077` (:139, const at :97), throws naming the literal `chmod 600 <path>` (:141-144). Called at :798 (`loadInitial`) and :872 (`reconcileFromDisk`, re-checked before every write). So the mechanism is described correctly.

KILL 1 — the win32 skip is necessity, not a stance, so the feature is inert where omp ships. MEASURED on this win32 box (Bun 1.4.2): a file written with `{mode: 0o600}` stats as 0o100666, `mode & 0o077` = 54, and `chmod(0o600)` returns success while leaving it 0o666. Directories also read 0o666. So without the guard it would refuse to start 100% of the time on Windows; with it, it provides zero protection there. omp ships omp-windows-x64.exe / omp-windows-arm64.exe and runs --smoke-test on a windows-11-arm runner (.github/workflows/ci.yml:810,821,1013,1030,1032). The only live surface is POSIX.

KILL 2 — omp already has the same idiom in a strictly better form and deliberately chose repair over refusal. `collab/registry.ts:393` runs the identical `(stat.mode & 0o077) !== 0` test but REPAIRS via `chmod(dir, 0o700)`; `assertPrivateDir` returns early on win32 (:375) before the mode read. omp's credential paths use best-effort chmod with a swallowed error: auth-broker-cli.ts:101-110, auth-gateway-cli.ts:87-96 and :113-118, sqlite-credential-store.ts:526-530. Porting a refusal replaces a coherent codebase-wide policy with a divergent one.

KILL 3 — a single-file check would not cover omp's credential store even on POSIX, so it would give false assurance. omp's store is SQLite in WAL mode (sqlite-credential-store.ts:570). MEASURED: writing a secret row and chmod'ing only the main db yields three files — auth.db, auth.db-wal (12392 B, holding the written secret bytes), auth.db-shm. omp chmods only dbPath. A ported assertOwnerOnly(filename) checks the main db and silently misses the -wal sidecar where the just-written token actually lives. A check that passes while the secret sits in an un-chmod'd sidecar is worse than no check.

KILL 4 — omp reads credential files it does not own; a refusal there is an unrecoverable outage. `packages/ai/src/providers/google-auth.ts:69-95` reads GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS (arbitrary path, :84) and ~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json (:70). omp neither creates nor chmods these. On shared runners, k8s secret mounts and NFS/SMB home dirs the group bit is structurally set; on some installs the user cannot chmod. The dsh error tells the user to chmod a file owned by another tool — possibly not permitted, and possibly breaking the gcloud CLI that owns it.

FROM THE HOME REPO'S OWN SIBLING: `packages/spill/spill-local/src/cleanup.ts:47-55,86-88` uses the same win32-skip idiom for the same problem class, but with the narrower `0o022` (write-by-others) instead of `0o077`, AND honors the sticky bit (`mode & 0o1000`) so /tmp per-process roots work. That is the more careful design in the same codebase, and it feeds a policy predicate rather than a boot refusal.

COVERAGE: the dsh refusal test is `it.skipIf(process.platform === 'win32')` (tests/local.spec.ts:170) and the win32 branch is bracketed by /* v8 ignore */ (src/index.ts:136,138,145) — the feature has zero executed coverage on Windows, exactly where it is inert.

## [v1]

reason: The claim inverts the actual mechanism. It asserts a "consumer-own-the-vocabulary split" where "the tool owns the operation-specific hint." The code shows the opposite: the shared unit (`packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/escalation.ts`) owns 100% of the hint TEXT, including the verbatim sentence the model must recognize. `escalationHintMarker(subject)` at escalation.ts:84-86 is a full template literal in the unit. Tools call it with a single one-word noun ('command' | 'operation'). A repo-wide grep for the hint literal `retry this exact` yields exactly ONE production site: escalation.ts:85 — zero tool-local constructions. So there is no split at all; it is a shared template with an injected noun.

Worse, the claim's own stated benefit is produced by the mechanism it denies. The claim says this design "keeps bash and fs from drifting apart." If the tool owned the hint, drift would be guaranteed. escalation.ts:7-8 says the opposite in the code's own words: "One home keeps the two families' approval ordering and verbatim error texts from drifting apart." Keeping the verbatim text in the unit IS the anti-drift mechanism. The claim names the effect and attributes it to an inverted cause.

Two secondary defects. (a) The line citation is wrong: `escalation.ts:1-8` is the module JSDoc and contains no marker or hint code; the file is 208 lines, with the marker at 71-73, the hint at 84-86, and the schema description at 95-97. (b) The scope is understated as "bash and fs" — four tool families consume the module: tool-bash, tool-pwsh, tool-fs, and tool-str-replace-editor (the last takes the denial marker only, index.ts:86).

What DOES hold is the dependency half: neither tool imports the other in `src/` (cross-references found are only self-referential `@module` JSDoc tags), and both depend on `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox`. escalation.ts:10-14 independently confirms this via the structural `EscalationAsk` seam, so the sandbox package never imports the approval or agent packages.

Correct characterization: a shared-template-with-injected-noun design. This is a genuinely strong pattern and arguably BETTER than what the claim describes — the invariant portion of the hint cannot drift at all, only the noun slot varies, and escalation.spec.ts:57-59 pins both variants. Tier if applied to omp: BORROW the pattern; DO-NOT-COPY this description of it.

Reality at C:/Users/ADMIN/Projects/deepseek-harness/packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/escalation.ts: the unit exports BOTH the marker (sandboxDenialMarker, :71) AND the hint (escalationHintMarker, :84) AND the schema description (sandboxPermissionsDescription, :95). The tools own only a one-word noun — 'command' (tool-bash, tool-pwsh) or 'operation' (tool-fs). The entire hint sentence, including "retry this exact X once with sandbox_permissions (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) + justification; the approval prompt asks the user", is composed INSIDE the unit at :85. There is no "tool owns the operation-specific hint" split to port. The literal parameter is `subject: string` — a noun, not a hint.

(2) THE CITATION IS WRONG AND SELF-CONTRADICTING. The path is packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/escalation.ts (208 lines), not sandbox/src/escalation.ts. Lines 1-8 are the module JSDoc, which never mentions a "consumer-own-the-vocabulary split" — and its actual closing sentence, :8, says "One home keeps the two families' approval ordering and verbatim error texts from drifting apart", i.e. the verbatim texts live in the UNIT. The claim quotes the one line that argues against it.

(3) THE PREMISE IS ABSENT FROM omp, AND omp ALREADY HAS A BETTER VERSION.
- grep for sandbox_permissions|WIDER_MODES|ESCALATION_TARGETS|escalationHint|approveEscalation|sandboxDenialMarker across packages/coding-agent/src/ = 0 hits. All 81 "sandbox" hits in omp are unrelated: git-worktree task-isolation dirs, SchemeWriteScope="sandbox" for internal-URL scratch roots (internal-urls/types.ts:75), a Google API hostname (agent-session.ts:11364). omp has no confinement layer, no SandboxMode, no wider ladder, no per-call escalation argument. Nothing to attach a vocabulary module to.
- The constraint that forced dsh's design is a package-boundary cycle. dsh's bash is packages/shell/tool-bash, fs is packages/fs/tool-fs, str-replace is packages/fs/tool-str-replace-editor, ptc is packages/core/tools — four workspace packages. That is why a 5th package (dsh-sandbox) is needed and why EscalationApprover<A,C> (:113-127) and EscalationOutcome (:104) are re-declared as a minimal STRUCTURAL shape to avoid importing the approval service. In omp, bash.ts, write.ts, ast-edit.ts, glob.ts, grep.ts all sit in the SAME directory src/tools/ of the SAME package @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent and all import ./approval directly. The cycle cannot form.
- omp already implements the pattern, and it is closer to the claim's wording than dsh's code. tools/approval.ts:1-8 states it outright: "Approval policy is declared by each tool. This module only knows how to: normalize user tools.approval overrides, compare a tool capability tier against the active approval mode, format the generic approval prompt body." denyError (:323) owns the shared denial marker; the tool owns `reason`. formatApprovalPrompt (:366) owns the shared body; the tool owns formatApprovalDetails?.(args) (:377). 9 real providers (bash.ts:562, write.ts:428, ast-edit.ts:166, debug.ts:550, eval.ts:349, ida.ts:87, edit/index.ts:395, lsp/tool.ts:178, task/index.ts:512).
- omp's chokepoint is tighter, which is the whole anti-drift point. omp applies the shared vocabulary at 2 call sites total (extensibility/extensions/wrapper.ts:369, eval/preludes.ts:111) for every tool including extension/hook-minted ones. dsh needs 18 non-definition call sites — 8 sandboxDenialMarker, 7 escalationHintMarker, 3 sandboxPermissionsDescription — across 9 files in 4 packages, each of which must independently remember to append the hint (tool-bash render.ts:46,49,113,115; tool-pwsh render.ts:69,135; tool-bash background.ts:26-27; tool-pwsh background.ts:29; tool-fs sandbox.ts:129; str-replace-editor index.ts:86). That 18-site fan-out IS the drift surface the claim praises; omp structurally does not have it.
- omo is empty: 0 hits for all six escalation identifiers in C:/Users/ADMIN/Projects/oh-my-openagent.

TIER: DO-NOT-COPY. Porting is net-negative — it requires inventing a confinement layer omp does not have, splitting a single-package tool directory into package boundaries to manufacture the very cycle the pattern exists to avoid, and adding a second, redundant vocabulary owner alongside tools/approval.ts, which would create the drift the claim is trying to prevent.

The proposed destination is likewise MIT (ultraworkers, "Copyright (c) 2025 Mario Zechner"), so MIT -> MIT is compatible and taking the CODE is clean; the sole obligation is retaining the DeepSeek copyright line in substantial portions. The code is also small and self-contained: 3 regex constants plus an 8-line resolveId, making copying a ~25-line job rather than a port. Verdict: BORROW the pattern, and the code is legally copyable. Two accuracy defects do not touch legality: (1) "18-entry allow-list" materially understates the real escape surface, because the gate has FOUR exemptions, two of them unbounded - isRequested (:538, per-package clientExternals set), VENDORED_LIBRARY (:72, cosmokit|schemastery), INLINE_SAFE (18 named), and GENERATED_REMOTE (:75), an open regex matching any future package's /remote subpath; (2) "type-only imports explicitly exempted" is prose in the error message, not a code branch - it is true only in effect because tsconfig.base.json:18 sets verbatimModuleSyntax:false so tsc elides first. Portability caveat if it is ever lifted: it keys on `source` alone and ignores `importer`, so a relative import reaching into another package's source bypasses the gate, and the code is coupled to dsh's scope prefix, its clientExternals module table, and cordis.

## [v3]

reason: REFUTED — but NOT on license grounds. The licensing is clean; the claim fails on PROVENANCE and on PRIOR ART.

1) PROVENANCE MISATTRIBUTION (decisive). The "accessibility-tree golden test" is not dsh's invention. scaffold.ts:1611 is `let previous = normalize(await region.ariaSnapshot())` — `ariaSnapshot()` is a Playwright built-in (Apache-2.0, Microsoft), and the golden format in snapshots/web/*/ui.expected.md is Playwright's own YAML (`- banner:`, `- button "X" [disabled] [expanded]`). dsh's own THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:238 records `playwright | Apache-2.0`. The claim credits DeepSeek for a Microsoft feature.

2) THE COPYABLE CODE DELTA IS ~151 LINES OF GENERIC TEST DISCIPLINE, NOT A TECHNIQUE. The dsh-authored surface is scaffold.ts:1540-1690 (normalizeAria 1540, captureStableAria 1589, captureExpandedTurnProcessAria 1622, compareOrRefreshGolden 1675) = 151 of 1761 lines in a file importing ~10 private `@deepseek-ai/*` workspace packages (apps/web/package.json:33-63). What it adds is settle-poll-until-two-captures-equal + volatile normalization + refresh-only-writer. That is transferable as an IDEA in ~10 lines, not as code worth lifting.

3) THE GOLDENS ARE NOT PORTABLE. 18 of 31 snapshots/web/*/ui.expected.md embed DeepSeek product surface ("DeepSeek Chat", "DeepSeek Reasoner", "deepseek/deepseek-chat", "deepseek/deepseek-reasoner"). Copying them into a public MIT repo imports a competitor's branded product output, and they encode DeepSeek's own UI tree — useless outside dsh.

4) PRIOR ART IN omp — omp ALREADY SHIPS THE ENTIRE CAPABILITY, INCLUDING BASELINE DIFFING. packages/coding-agent/src/tools/browser/aria/aria-snapshot.bundle.txt:1-2 is a committed bundle of Playwright v1.61.0's aria snapshot, correctly attributed "(Apache-2.0, (c) Microsoft)", regenerated by scripts/generate-aria-snapshot.ts:26-41 from 7 pinned upstream files. aria-snapshot.ts:52,157,167 injects it; cmux-tab.ts:934-947 already does `diffAriaSnapshot(this.#ariaSnapshotBaselines, key, this.#lastUrl, snapshot)` against a `#ariaSnapshotBaselines` Map (cmux-tab.ts:562). Plus a11y/audit.ts (339 lines) and aria-snapshot.ts (168 lines). The proposed borrow is already in the codebase, properly licensed.

HONEST COUNTERWEIGHT (why confidence is medium, not high): there is NO license defect. dsh is MIT "Copyright (c) 2026 DeepSeek", origin = official github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness, 73 contributors, 317 commits on scaffold.ts, no CLA, no export restriction (SAFETY.md:22 explicitly says "provided without warranty under the MIT License"), no per-file SPDX overrides. MIT→MIT copying of the 151-line wrapper is legally clean. The refutation is that the claim describes a Microsoft feature as a DeepSeek innovation, and proposes borrowing something omp already has.

TIER: REFERENCE at best, effectively IDEA-ONLY. The "Accessibility-tree golden tests instead of pixel/DOM diffs" premise is unsound on its own terms — omp's aria snapshots are for LLM agent consumption, not regression goldens, so a golden-diff harness over them would be a misuse of the feature, not an upgrade. DO-NOT-COPY the goldens and the scaffold (it will not compile outside dsh's private workspace). BORROW, at most, the ~15-line concept: poll a snapshot until two consecutive normalized captures are equal before asserting, because a single-shot capture races the last React commits.

EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED (temp spec I ran against the real preset, then deleted; repo left clean):
- Real tsdown/rolldown build, `import { X } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'` → build fails with the purity error.
- `import type { X } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'` → build succeeds. `export type { X } from ...` → succeeds.
- `import { type X, Y } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'` → build FAILS (a mixed specifier is a value import, correctly gated).
- `import('@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent')` dynamic → build fails.
- `import { x } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-deque'` (INLINE_SAFE) → succeeds.
- Shipped spec `scripts/client-bundle-purity.spec.ts` — 40 tests, all pass in 1.11s.
- The type-only exemption is load-bearing, not theoretical: 3050 `import type ... from '@deepseek-ai/...'` lines exist across `packages/*/*/src`.

WHERE THE CLAIM IS OVERSTATED (scope, not mechanism):
1. Coverage is 71 of the 78 packages that import the preset. The gate lives ONLY in `clientConfig()` (:473), reachable only through `clientBundle()` (:119). The 7 that import the preset but never call `clientBundle()` get NO gate: `packages/client/store`, `ui-dockkit`, `ui-primitives`, `ui-slots`, `web` (all `staticLinked`) and `packages/test-support/{client-runtime,remote-mock}` (`clientLibrary`). `apps/web/vite.config.ts` has no `resolveId` gate either — the only `resolveId` hit under `apps/` is an e2e test helper at `apps/web/tests/focus-rings.e2e.ts:258`. So "the UI must not reach into the kernel" is true for the dynamically-loaded plugin channel, NOT for the static-assembly channel or the shell. It is more precisely a plugin-isolation rule.
2. It is not a hard "no" — it is "declare it". 5 packages buy admission via `dsh.client.external` in package.json (api/job-controller, api/session-controller, api/terminal-controller, api/workspace-controller, experimental/client-ui-voice-input), all requesting `@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-gateway/client`. The gate message itself says so.
3. "18-entry allow-list" describes `INLINE_SAFE` alone. The full admitted set adds two WILDCARD patterns: `VENDORED_LIBRARY` (:72, `cosmokit|schemastery`, any subpath) and `GENERATED_REMOTE` (:75, `^@deepseek-ai/dsh-[a-z0-9-]*/remote$`, matching ANY package name whether or not a `/remote` subpath exists). The spec pins that wildcard as deliberate (`scripts/client-bundle-purity.spec.ts:159-164`).
4. "Type-only explicitly exempted" needs one correction: the plugin has NO `isTypeOnly` branch. The exemption is emergent, not coded — rolldown runs the oxc/tsc transform before resolving dependencies, so `import type` is already gone when `resolveId` would fire. In the CI Client face the entry is `lib/types/client/index.js` (:118), i.e. tsc output, so erasure happened even earlier. Proof it is the transform and not the gate: when I put `import type` into a `.js` entry I got `[PARSE_ERROR] Expected from but found {`, not a purity pass.

DO-NOT-COPY / REFERENCE: the two wildcard escape hatches are the part not worth copying blind — `GENERATED_REMOTE` is an open-ended admission keyed on a naming convention rather than an enumerated entry, so a package can be made inline-able by adding a `remote` subpath. The ~18-line enumerated `INLINE_SAFE` is the better discipline; the wildcard would defeat it.

Gate site — packages/client/tsdown.client.ts:528-546 (verbatim):
  plugins: [{
    // Bundle purity gate (build-time mirror of the module-edge rules): the
    // baseline and package-specific requests stay external, inline-safe wire layers
    // inline, and every other @deepseek-ai value import is a build error — ...
    name: 'dsh-client-bundle-purity',
    resolveId(source: string) {
      if (!source.startsWith('@deepseek-ai/')) return null
      if (isRequested(source)) return null // requested module-table row: external wins
      if (VENDORED_LIBRARY.test(source)) return null

        + '(type-only imports are erased and never reach this gate)',

    },
  }, ...]

## [v1]

reason: The TECHNICAL CLAIM IS ACCURATE — confirmed verbatim in code, not refuted. But its source attribution is wrong, and it under-describes the helper.

WHAT IS CONFIRMED (every element, from code):
1. "capture, then poll until two consecutive normalized captures are equal" — apps/web/tests/scaffold.ts:1611-1617. `let previous = normalize(await region.ariaSnapshot())`, then `expect.poll(async () => { const current = normalize(await region.ariaSnapshot()); const stable = current === previous; previous = current; return stable }).toBe(true)`. The rolling `previous = current` makes it require two consecutive EQUAL normalized captures. This is a real poll, not a hot loop: playwright/lib/matchers/expect.js:12961 confirms `pollAgainstDeadline2(..., poll.intervals ?? [100, 250, 500, 1e3])`.
2. "named timeout message" — scaffold.ts:1617, verbatim `{ timeout: 5_000, message: 'aria snapshot did not stabilize' }`.
3. "Solves the React commit race" — stated as intent in the doc comment, scaffold.ts:1573-1575: "poll until two consecutive normalized captures are equal — a single-shot capture races the last React commits." Independently corroborated elsewhere in the repo, not just this comment: .agents/notes/implemented/testing/2026-07-24-web-gui-browser-e2e-lane.md:31 ("No single-shot transient-DOM assertions ... sampling `[data-streaming]` is a race by construction") and apps/web/tests/navigation-panes.e2e.ts:186 ("The API baselines can settle before React commits their projection").
4. SCALE: 339 references across 96 files, with exactly ONE implementation (`function captureStableAria` appears once, at scaffold.ts:1589). Not a one-off pattern.

WHERE THE CLAIM IS IMPRECISE (does not rise to refutation):
- SOURCE PATH IS WRONG. "dsh/client-ui-interaction" does not exist — no dir, no file, and `grep -ril "client-ui-interaction"` over the whole repo (excl. node_modules) returns zero hits. `packages/interaction/` exists but is server-side (commands, permission-presets, tool-ask-user, user-approval, user-questions). Real location: apps/web/tests/scaffold.ts:1589. This is a citation error, not a mechanism error — the mechanism is unambiguous.
- UNDER-DESCRIBES the helper. It also does a large normalization pass (normalizeAria, scaffold.ts:1540-1570: uuid, cwd, workspace-basename, duration, throughput, clock, timestamp, compaction tokens) and a DEFAULT pre-wait for the background-jobs control to detach (1599-1602, 10s), with a `runningJobs: 'keep'` escape hatch. The claim reduces it to polling.
- SCOPE IS ARIA-ONLY. The repo has ZERO `toHaveScreenshot` golden assertions; `page.screenshot` is only used for CI evidence artifacts, never asserted. So the pattern does not generalize to pixel/image snapshots.
- "SOLVES" IS HEURISTIC, NOT GUARANTEED. Two equal samples can occur at a mid-render quiescent moment (false-stable), and a settle slower than the 5s cap hard-fails. It is a bounded quiescence detector. The repo's own .agents/skills/dsh-ci-test-reliability/SKILL.md cuts both ways on this: it says "Use a timeout only to bound a wait, never as the condition that makes the assertion correct" (satisfied — the condition is the equality, the timeout only bounds it), but it also lists "adding retries" under "Reject flake-masking fixes" for deterministic local tests. The helper sits in that gray zone, though it names the awaited condition rather than blindly re-running, which is what the skill's own carve-out requires.

BOTTOM LINE: BORROW the pattern (poll-until-two-equal + named timeout message is genuinely good practice for golden a11y snapshots), but correct the citation to apps/web/tests/scaffold.ts:1589 and do not generalize it to image snapshots or treat it as a race-proof guarantee.

export async function captureStableAria(page, selector, workspaceCwd, options = {}) {
  if ((options.runningJobs ?? 'settle') === 'settle') {
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /background jobs? running/ })
      .waitFor({ state: 'detached', timeout: 10_000 })
  }
  const region = page.locator(selector).first()
  const normalize = (snapshot) => { /* replacements */ return normalizeAria(snapshot, workspaceCwd, age) }
  let previous = normalize(await region.ariaSnapshot())
  await expect.poll(async () => {
    const current = normalize(await region.ariaSnapshot())
    const stable = current === previous
    previous = current
    return stable
  }, { timeout: 5_000, message: 'aria snapshot did not stabilize' }).toBe(true)
  return previous
}

## [v2]

reason: REFUTED on portability. The claim accurately describes dsh, but the invariant it enforces is INVERTED in omp, the failure mode it defends against does not occur at omp's build boundary (and omp already fixed the version of it that does occur, at runtime), and omp already owns both the build mechanism and a stronger runtime enforcement. Porting the gate shape would be a net regression: it converts a fail-closed 18-entry allow-list into a fail-open 3,744-edge one, and would cost 475 lines of test for a 0-edge, 2-specifier rule that oxlint enforces in ~15.

(1) INVERTED INVARIANT. The rationale "the UI must not reach into the kernel" is false in omp — the TUI *is* a kernel consumer by design. packages/tui/src/overlays/pause-screen.ts:14 value-imports `agentPauseGate`, a module-level singleton at packages/agent/src/pause.ts:107 (`export const agentPauseGate = new AgentPauseGate()`). tui carries 13 non-type pi-agent-core edges plus 59 pi-ai, 123 pi-utils, 26 pi-natives, 16 pi-catalog. The direction omp forbids — kernel reaching up into tui/coding-agent — is already 0 real value edges (my grep found 3 hits across ai/utils/wire; all three are comments: packages/ai/src/providers/cursor.ts:1697, packages/utils/src/format.ts:79, packages/wire/src/index.ts:4). A gate written to dsh's spec would force-allowlist the exact edges the claim says must be forbidden.

(2) THE MOTIVATING HAZARD IS ABSENT AT omp's BUILD BOUNDARY, AND BLIND TO omp's REAL ONE. dsh's duplicate-instance risk comes from plugin bundles loaded as closures through a module table (`window.__ModuleLoader__.load({id, factory})`, cordis DI — packages/client/modules/src/client/manifest.ts:1-25). omp emits ONE entrypoint per build (bundle-dist.ts:88 `entrypoints: [src/cli.ts]`; compile-binary.ts:42), so no plugin closure exists to duplicate an instance. But omp DOES ship real double-instance bugs — at the *runtime* extension boundary, from disk-loaded extensions: packages/coding-agent/test/issue-6449-legacy-pi-cjs-double-instance.test.ts:1-33 records a second `legacy-pi-compat` instance with empty graph state, repaired by a global first-wins registry (`__ompLegacyPiRequireGraphModule`). A build-time gate inspects the compiled graph and is structurally blind to an instance created by re-evaluating a host module from disk on a source-link install. The gate would have passed green and #6449 would still have shipped. This is the decisive refutation: the tool cannot see the failure mode omp actually experiences.

(3) omp ALREADY HAS BOTH MECHANISMS, AND THE RUNTIME ONE IS STRONGER. Build-time module-edge plugin: packages/coding-agent/scripts/legacy-pi-virtual-module.ts:199-205 (Bun.build `onResolve`/`onLoad`, 208 lines), wired via createLegacyPiVirtualModulePlugin() in bundle-dist.ts:7. So the mechanism ports; the *use* is already taken. Runtime mirror: withHostGuard (packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/utils.ts:118-196) fences process.exit, process.reallyExit, all five stdin events, and raw/paused state around extension evaluation — strictly stronger than an edge gate because it constrains *effects*, not just edges, and it is pinned to shipped issues (#5618 stdin hijack, #6488 signal handlers). ## [v2]

reason: VERDICT: REFUTED as a port. The claim is ACCURATE about dsh, but it does not survive the port to omp, and omp already solves the underlying concern by a strictly better mechanism where it exists.

=== SOURCE VERIFIED (claim is true at home) ===
`C:/Users/ADMIN/Projects/deepseek-harness/apps/web/tests/scaffold.ts:1589-1619`, `captureStableAria()`. It does exactly what the claim says: seeds `previous` with one normalized capture, then `expect.poll(...)` until `current === previous`, with `{ timeout: 5_000, message: 'aria snapshot did not stabilize' }` (lines 1612-1617). The doc comment at 1573-1575 states the rationale verbatim: "poll until two consecutive normalized captures are equal — a single-shot capture races the last React commits."
SCALE (honest): the helper is load-bearing, not incidental — 350 call sites across 98 distinct test files, out of 156 web e2e test files in `apps/web/tests/`. It also carries a 30-line `normalizeAria()` (scaffold.ts:1540-1570) collapsing uuid/cwd/duration/throughput/timestamps to tokens, and a `runningJobs: 'settle'|'keep'` gate (1599-1602) because a foreground shell job's removal reaches the browser "one coalesced roster frame after the tool result." In a live-browser Playwright harness against a streaming React app, that is a real race and this is a real fix. REFERENCE tier, not DO-NOT-COPY-in-general.

=== WHY THE PORT FAILS — four measured blockers ===

(1) omp has no Playwright, and the pattern is built on three Playwright-only APIs.
- `grep -rl "playwright" --include=package.json packages/ package.json` -> 0 files. No manifest declares it.
- `ls -d node_modules/playwright* node_modules/@playwright` -> absent. omp drives browsers with `puppeteer-core@25.3.0` (package.json:59), used by `packages/browser-relay` and the coding-agent browser tool.
- The helper needs `expect.poll()`, `locator.ariaSnapshot()`, and Playwright's `expect`. omp runs `bun test` (package.json:85 -> `scripts/ci-test-ts.ts`). `grep -c "poll" node_modules/bun-types/test.d.ts` -> 0. bun:test has no `expect.poll`.
- Exact `grep -rn "expect\.poll" packages/` (escaped dot) -> **0 hits**. My first pass reported apparent hits; those were false positives from an unescaped `.` matching `expect(polls)` (confirmed at `packages/agent/test/agent-loop.test.ts:3414`). Correcting for it: zero.

(2) omp's React tests have no commit race to solve — and already use the better tool.
- All 4 `.tsx` tests in `packages/collab-web/test/` (`composer`, `markdown`, `tool-view`, `transcript`) use `renderToStaticMarkup` from `react-dom/server` (imports at composer.test.tsx:3, markdown.test.tsx:2, tool-view.test.tsx:2, transcript.test.tsx:3). That is a synchronous single-pass pure function: same props -> same string, one pass, no commit phase, no effects, no reconciliation. A poll cannot observe a race that has no commit boundary.
- The ONE client-mount test, `packages/stats/test/errors-route-range.test.tsx`, wraps every render in `await act(async () => { root?.render(...) })` (lines 32, 66-68, 73) with `IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT` set (line 57). Same in `packages/utils/test/dom.test.ts:175-176`.
- This is the decisive point: `act()` makes the commit boundary deterministic and flushes effects before the assertion. Polling is the fallback for when you cannot control the commit boundary. Importing a poll into a codebase that already has `act()` would be a REGRESSION — it trades a deterministic 0-flake seam for a wall-clock timeout that can still flake.

(3) omp's only real-Chromium a11y test has no async DOM.
`packages/coding-agent/test/tools/browser-a11y.test.ts` is the single test that launches actual Chromium and runs an accessibility audit. Its fixture (lines 40-51) is static hand-authored HTML — `<img>`, `<div>`, `<section>`, `<iframe srcdoc>` — with zero JS-driven mutation. The audit is a pure function over a settled DOM. There is nothing to poll for.

(4) The directory the task names has no UI in it.
`packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/` = 3,939 lines across 12 `.ts` files plus `extensions/`, `plugins/`, `hooks/`, `custom-commands/`, `custom-tools/`. It is the extension/plugin API: loaders, runners, settings, skills, slash commands, and legacy pi-* shims. Grepping it for `snapshot|aria|poll|react|stabil` yields only unrelated hits: a `ReviewDiffSnapshot` git-diff type (`custom-commands/bundled/review/diff.ts:10`), a `/\.snap$/` file-extension filter (diff.ts:31), and `tui.requestRender()` calls. No React, no a11y tree, no snapshot test, no DOM.

=== HARD RULE 3 CHECKED: does the concept live elsewhere under another name? YES — and it is already right ===
The aria-snapshot concept IS in omp, under a different name and a different role. `packages/coding-agent/src/tools/browser/aria/aria-snapshot.ts` vendors Playwright's OWN ARIA-snapshot sources as a committed bundle (`aria-snapshot.bundle.txt`, pinned tag, Apache-2.0; see the header comment at lines 9-14) and runs them inside Puppeteer's isolated world. But that is a runtime agent capability, not test infra, and it is deliberately single-shot: `captureAriaSnapshot()` (line 65) does one `page.evaluate` and returns. It does not poll — the design is that the agent re-captures on demand rather than the tool guessing when the page settled. omp's test for it (`packages/coding-agent/test/tools/browser-aria-snapshot.test.ts`, 108 lines) tests pure functions over string fixtures — `parseAriaRefSelector`, `postProcessAriaSnapshot`, `diffAriaSnapshot` — with no page and no race. So even where the concept exists, it has already been designed and tested without polling.

=== HONEST COUNTERWEIGHT: omp does poll where polling is correct ===

reason: ACCURATE, not overstated, and not merely a narrow case — though it holds at ONE level of the disclosure hierarchy.

WHAT I CONFIRMED (all from code, not docs — grep over docs/, AGENTS.md, packages/client/AGENTS.md for this doctrine returned ZERO hits, so the pattern exists only as a code contract, never as a written rule):

1. A named helper implements exactly the claim. `captureExpandedTurnProcessAria` at `apps/web/tests/scaffold.ts:1630-1665`. Its own doc comment (scaffold.ts:1621-1623) states the claim verbatim: "Capture stable aria with every eligible Turn process and secondary group expanded, then restore the controls that were closed before the capture."

2. The implementation matches the prose. scaffold.ts:1636 selects `[data-turn-process], [data-process-activity]`; :1640-1645 clicks every visible control whose `aria-expanded === 'false'` and records each index in `opened`; :1658 captures; :1659-1663 restores in a `finally` block, re-clicking in reverse order. The restore is in `finally`, so it survives a capture throw. Reverse-order restore is the correct instinct (undo LIFO).

3. SCALE (measured, not estimated): 19 call sites across 17 e2e files (`rg -c "await captureExpandedTurnProcessAria\("`). All 17 of those files also call `compareOrRefreshGolden` — every single call site feeds a golden. 15 dedicated `*-expanded.expected.md` goldens exist on disk, each paired with a default-state sibling.

4. The "covers the full content" effect is real and measurable, not rhetorical. `diff snapshots/web/seeded-history/ui.expected.md snapshots/web/seeded-history/ui-expanded.expected.md` shows the default golden's lone line `- button "Took {{duration}}"` becoming `- button "Took {{duration}}" [expanded]` plus 9 previously-invisible lines (Read files group, two Think blocks, two Read tool rows with content). 13 diff lines. subagent-conversation: 41 -> 45 lines. live-interactions/retry: 26 -> 30. seeded-history/ui: 30 -> 39.

5. The restore is load-bearing, not decorative — two independent in-code corroborations. (a) `present.e2e.ts:196-199` calls `captureExpandedTurnProcessAria` and then `await expandTurnProcesses(page)` on the very NEXT line, which is a no-op unless the restore actually re-collapsed the controls. (b) `skill-user-invoke.e2e.ts:143-152` captures a default-state golden, then an expanded golden, from the same live page.

SCOPE CAVEATS (narrowing, not refuting):
- The helper covers only TWO of at least FOUR disclosure attribute families. It does not touch `[data-disclosure-row]` (the shared primitive, packages/client/ui-primitives/src/DisclosureRow.tsx:81, used by tool cards, WorkflowRunPanel, cordis rows) or `[data-expandable]` (per-tool cards: read/terminal/web cards, tool-call-tree). `code-language.snapshot.ts:64,81` must hand-toggle `[data-disclosure-row]` itself precisely because the helper would not. So "expand before capture" is complete only at the turn-summary/group level; deeper per-tool disclosures are still manual.
- A sibling helper `expandTurnProcesses` (apps/web/tests/support.ts:128-136) performs the same expansion with NO restore, and is used in 10 files — 9 of which also compare goldens (workflow-run, thinking-markdown, present, replay-round-trip, code-language, diff-context, clickable-links-gallery, bash-abort-row, question-composer). So the restore half is the dominant convention, not an invariant.
- Latent fragility, not a refutation: the restore re-resolves `controls.nth(index)` AFTER the capture (scaffold.ts:1661), so if disclosure controls were inserted or reordered mid-capture, the restore could hit the wrong element.

TIER: BORROW the helper wholesale — it is ~35 lines, has no repo-specific coupling, and the paired-golden shape (default golden + `*-expanded.expected.md` golden from the same page) is a strictly better artifact than a single golden. REFERENCE the `finally`-based restore discipline for any other expand/capture helper added later. DO-NOT-COPY the index-based restore as written; keying the restore on a stable id (e.g. `data-chat-turn`) rather than a positional index would remove the DOM-reorder hazard.

## [v2]

reason: REFUTED on portability. The claim is TRUE in dsh — I verified both cited anchors exactly. But every load-bearing half of it is either a shipped capability omp already has in a richer form, an invariant omp deliberately asserts in tests, or a defense against a failure mode that cannot occur in omp's code shape. A straight port is net-negative on 4 of 4 clauses.

(1) "'allowed-once' is the ONLY grant" would DELETE two shipped grant kinds. omp already ships persistent grants: acp-permission-gate.ts:15-20 offers allow_once/allow_always/reject_once/reject_always; client-bridge.ts:34 types all four; session-tools.ts:990-994 persists allow_always/reject_always into #acpPermissionDecisions, and :939-945 short-circuits on them. dsh's 4-value union cannot even EXPRESS reject_always — so a port loses an allow-always AND a reject-always. That is a safety regression, not an import.

(2) "A missing answerer denies" is ALREADY VIOLATED in omp, and the violation is an asserted contract, not a bug. session-tools.ts:905 — `if (!bridge?.capabilities.requestPermission || !bridge.requestPermission) return tool;` returns the tool UNWRAPPED, so bash/edit/delete/move skip the gate entirely. agent-session-acp-permission.test.ts:5-6 states this as intended ("regular file-editing tools keep the same no-approval behavior they have in the TUI") and :383 "edit, write, and ast_edit do not request ACP permission" locks it in. Making it fail-closed is a product decision, not a port.

(3) The seam type is incommensurable — this is the core reason the containment machinery does not survive. dsh's fail-closed exists to contain an ASYNC, ORDERED, PLUGGABLE, UNTRUSTED chain: ctx.waterfall('approval/request', ...) at index.ts:281-284. omp's resolution is a SYNCHRONOUS TOTAL PURE FUNCTION — resolveApproval(tool, args, mode, userConfig) -> ResolvedApproval, approval.ts:203-318. No I/O, no dispatch, nothing to be missing, nothing to throw. Every dsh mechanism has no counterpart failure: the Promise.resolve().then() pre-entry (:280-284) defends a sync-throw that a pure function cannot produce; the rogue-return normalization (:288) defends a return that is already a closed literal union; the waterfall fallback (:283) defends a dispatch that does not exist. Porting = dead defense plus a vocabulary to reconcile.

(4) The vocabulary axes are orthogonal, not parallel. omp composes three independent axes — policy allow|deny|prompt (approval.ts:16), tier read|write|exec (agent/src/types.ts:988; approval.ts:96), mode always-ask|write|yolo (approval.ts:17) through a mode→max-tier table (approval.ts:120-124) — plus force-prompt `override: true` (types.ts:1016) and `policyKey` sub-tool scoping (types.ts:1018-1022). dsh has none of these; it is a flat 4-value union. A flat union cannot represent "prompt because tier=exec under mode=write, unless override". Collapsing to dsh's shape deletes the tier system that xdevTierResolved (wrapper.ts:291) and xdevBypass (wrapper.ts:302) depend on.

(5) The default is INVERTED. dsh defaults policy 'ask' with fail-closed fallback (index.ts:152, :244). omp defaults tools.approvalMode to "yolo" (tools/settings.ts:294) AND falls back to "yolo" on an invalid or missing value (approval.ts:80). Importing dsh's posture flips every existing omp user from allow-everything to ask-everything.

(6) The TUI prompt is 2-value, not 4-value. wrapper.ts:376 — uiContext.select(safetyPrompt, ["Approve", "Deny"]). reason: REFUTED as a port. The claim is accurate about dsh (citation checks out: user-approval/src/index.ts:84-92 is `hasOpenTurn`, :217-223 is the throw, :225-232 is the `approval/asked`+`approval/decided` append pair), but it does not survive the port, because all three of its load-bearing preconditions are absent or deliberately inverted in omp. Measured:

(1) THERE IS NO DURABLE TURN BOUNDARY TO ENCLOSE. dsh's precondition exists *only* because dsh's log treats the turn as the commit/replay boundary (index.ts:78-83: "a bare event appended between turns is indistinguishable from a crash tail and silently dropped on reload"). omp's `turn_start`/`turn_end` are ephemeral extension notifications emitted via `#extensionRunner.emit` (session/agent-session.ts:4655-4665) and are never appended to the session log — `grep -n "appendEntry\|append(" agent-session.ts | grep -i turn` returns 0 hits. omp's durable `SessionEntry` union (session/session-entries.ts:36-291: session, message, model_usage, thinking_level_change, model_change, service_tier_change, compaction, branch_summary, reset_boundary, custom, label, title_change, ttsr_injection, credential_pin, session_init, mode_change, custom_message) contains no turn marker. `hasOpenTurn()` has nothing to scan for; porting it means first inventing a turn-commit boundary in the log, which is a different and much larger project than a pattern transfer.

(2) omp CHOSE THE OPPOSITE APPEND-FAILURE CONTRACT, ON PURPOSE. dsh's rule is "a failure that prevents either audit append from committing still rejects" (index.ts:205-206) plus "an authoritative append cannot reject the request" (index.ts:207-209) — append failure ⇒ refuse to answer. omp's `SessionStorageWriter` doc says the opposite verbatim (session/session-storage.ts:40-46): `appendSync` exists "so `SessionManager` can latch the first write failure before the appending call returns (surfaced by a later flushSync/close/next append — **the turn loop does not throw from append**)". The impl (session-storage.ts:285-307) writes in-body with `fs.writeSync` + `ftruncateSync` rollback precisely so "a software crash after the call still sees the entry." omp's stated goal is *never lose a committed entry*; dsh's is *refuse the decision if the log can't take it*. Porting "refuse when the audit cannot commit" would invert a documented invariant and require reworking the turn loop's error handling.

(3) THE RATIONALE EVAPORATES. Nothing is "silently dropped" in omp, because there is no turn commit to drop against — appends are in-body durable immediately (no fsync). A torn final record is bounded, not mistaken for a valid event: session/session-loader.ts:218 `if (read === 0) break; // incomplete record awaiting more data`.

HONEST NUANCE (what survives): the *underlying concern is real in omp* — approval decisions are never durably audited. `tool_approval_requested`/`tool_approval_resolved` (extensibility/extensions/wrapper.ts:327-346) are in-process `runner.emit` events to extension handlers, not log appends, and are **conditionally** emitted: `if (!hasApprovalHandlers) return;` (wrapper.ts:323-324, :338) means with no extension subscribed, zero audit events exist. `grep -rn "approval_decided\|approval/decided\|approval_asked\|approval/asked" --include=*.ts src` → 0 hits; the only `appendEntry("permissions", ...)` match is a docstring example (extensibility/hooks/types.ts:539). Per HARD RULE 3 I checked the concept under other names: `auditTrail|audit_log|decisionLog|decision_log|ledger` in session/ returns only spend/billing ledgers (agent-session.ts:10494, session-advisors.ts:638/671, unexpected-stop-classifier.ts:39) — unrelated. And the "fail closed + explain why" half of the claim omp ALREADY has, and well: wrapper.ts:351-366 fails closed with no UI and emits a user-actionable message listing three concrete remedies. So omp needs durability, but not dsh's mechanism.

TIERS: DO-NOT-COPY — the `hasOpenTurn()` precondition and the refuse-on-append-failure contract (inverts omp's documented append-error invariant; scan target does not exist). REFERENCE — the index.ts:78-83 rationale comment is a good template for *why* a durable log needs an enclosure invariant, worth reading only if omp ever adds a turn-commit boundary. BORROW (small, separable, but NOT the claimed pattern) — if omp wants approval audit durability, the portable move is a plain durable `custom` SessionEntry appended on every resolved decision, unconditional (drop the `hasApprovalHandlers` gate at wrapper.ts:326/:338 so the record exists regardless of subscription). That is a real gap with a different fix than the claim describes.

SCALE (measured, not estimated): dsh user-approval src = 515 LOC / 3 files (index.ts 310, invariant.ts 112, types.ts 93) + 626 LOC tests. omp approval surface = 528 LOC (tools/approval.ts 387 + session/acp-permission-gate.ts 141). omp extensibility total = 21,376 LOC. Comparable size, structurally unrelated: dsh's approval is a cordis Service coupled to a session log; omp's is a wrapper-level gate with pluggable storage (file/memory/SQL/Redis).

reason: The claim survives verification. I read all 74 lines of `C:/Users/ADMIN/Projects/deepseek-harness/apps/desktop/src/update-attention.ts`, its 81-line spec, and the sole caller's authorization path. Every one of the six asserted mechanics is present at the cited code, and two of them ("never steals focus", "attention never grants authorization") hold STRICTTER than the claim states — the latter is structurally enforced, not merely asserted in the header comment.

Three qualifications that qualify but do not refute:
1. "one reminder per version" is really "at most ONE ATTEMPT per version" and a focus-skip permanently BURNS the version. Line 25 stamps `this.version = version` BEFORE the focus check at line 26, so if the window is focused at ready() time, no notification fires AND the version is marked handled forever — no reminder even after the user backgrounds the app. Deliberate and tested (spec:59-65 asserts `notices).toHaveLength(0)` after unfocusing and re-calling ready()). The claim's upper bound is accurate; it just understates a lossy edge.
2. "platform-appropriate" covers 2 of 3 desktop platforms. Lines 38-39 branch only on `win32` (flashFrame) and `darwin` (dock.bounce). Linux has no branch at all — `app.dock` is undefined there, so Linux users get only the OS notification and no taskbar/urgency signal.
3. `silent: true` is macOS-honored. electron.d.ts:10557 documents that on Windows several properties "e.g., `actions`, `silent`, `icon`" are not available. Real option, best-effort cross-platform.

Scale (rule 4): 74 lines, one of 58 .ts files in apps/desktop/src, added in a single commit 63dd8fb80d. Not narrow-only.

Rule 3 check: this is the ONLY attention/notification site in the whole src tree (grepped `flashFrame|dock.bounce|new Notification|isSupported()` across apps/desktop/src — 5 hits, all in this file). Not one of several competing mechanisms.

Tiers: BORROW — the icon-first ordering at 37-40 before the `Notification.isSupported()` guard at 42, so taskbar attention survives notification rejection (tested, spec:73-81); the `stop` closure that owns focus-listener teardown so no listener leaks; the revision-counter authorization protocol (mandatory-update-window.ts:62,126 + 82-85). REFERENCE — the whole confirm/revision surface; omp is a CLI/TUI with no equivalent. DO-NOT-COPY — the skip-if-focused concept verbatim: omo is a terminal app where the window is always "focused", so that guard would fire on every update and silently produce zero reminders. A straight regression.

reason: The claim is REAL IN SUBSTANCE BUT MATERIALLY OVERSTATED, and I mark it refuted as written. Line 531 is exactly `realpath`, and it does gate the only client-path comparison in the module — but the claim's universal quantifiers ("before ANY equality check", "client-supplied paths") are contradicted by the code. Three measured defects: (1) `sameDirectory` has a live catch branch at index.ts:533-534 that performs a purely LEXICAL `resolve(left) === resolve(right)` equality check with no realpath whatsoever — the function's own docstring at :527 admits this ("Compare existing directories by physical identity and missing paths lexically"), so realpath is NOT unconditional; (2) it is a CHECK, not a CANONICALIZATION — the raw client string flows downstream unchanged (`cwd: params.cwd` at :208 and :259), the realpath'd value is discarded, and nothing pins the resolved target between check and use (TOCTOU); (3) the whole mechanism is UNTESTED — the only cwd assertions (bridge.spec.ts:220-224, :403) cover plain mismatch, and the single normalization case (bridge.spec.ts:229) passes identically under BOTH branches because resolve() normalizes `..` too. Scope is also narrower than stated: exactly ONE param field (`cwd`, 15 refs), not "client-supplied paths". BORROW with the caveat: the realpath-before-compare idea is sound and worth taking, but copy it as a two-branch helper with a real symlink test, not as a blanket guarantee.
evidence: FILE/LINE FACTS (all verified by reading code):
- Real path is `packages/acp/acp/src/index.ts` (536 lines), NOT `acp/src/index.ts`. Line 531 = `const [realLeft, realRight] = await Promise.all([realpath(left), realpath(right)])`. The location is accurate.
- `grep -c realpath packages/acp/acp/src/*.ts` => index.ts:2 (import at :15, call at :531), every other file 0. It is the ONLY realpath in the whole 7-file acp src.
- `grep -rn sameDirectory` => 3 call sites: :252, :271, :314 (resumeSession x2, listSessions). All cwd comparisons route through it.
- `grep -o "params\.[a-zA-Z]*"` => cwd 15, sessionId 5, additionalDirectories 3, mcpServers 2, value 1, cursor 1, configId 1. So `cwd` is the ONLY client-supplied path ever compared; `additionalDirectories` is rejected outright at :517-524, never compared. No `startsWith` prefix check anywhere in acp src.

REFUTATION 1 — "before ANY equality check" is literally false. index.ts:527-536 (verbatim):
  /** Compare existing directories by physical identity and missing paths lexically. */
  async function sameDirectory(left, right) {
    if (left === undefined) return false
    try { const [realLeft, realRight] = await Promise.all([realpath(left), realpath(right)])
          return realLeft === realRight
    } catch (_unresolvablePath) { return resolve(left) === resolve(right) }
  }
The catch branch is a purely LEXICAL equality check with zero realpath. git log -L 527,536 shows this was added in 511181684c "feat(acp): complete standard v1 automation controls".

REFUTATION 2 — check, not canonicalization. The raw client string is what is used downstream, not the realpath'd value: index.ts:259 `cwd: params.cwd` (resumeSession) and :208 `cwd: params.cwd` (newSession). The canonical form is thrown away; nothing pins the target between check and use.

REFUTATION 3 — UNTESTED. `grep -c "symlink\|realpath" packages/acp/acp/tests/*.ts` => 0 hits in all 7 test files. Only cwd assertions are bridge.spec.ts:220-224 and :403 (plain mismatch). The one normalization case, bridge.spec.ts:227-231 `cwd: ${process.cwd()}/packages/..`, resolves to HaveProperty('configOptions') — but it passes under BOTH branches, since `resolve()` normalizes `..` lexically too. No test distinguishes realpath from the lexical fallback.

PROBES I RAN (node v24.14.1, Windows): reimplemented sameDirectory verbatim and exercised it with a directory junction. `resolve(client) = ...\repo` confirmed lexical-only normalization; the `..`-through-nonexistent case MATCHED. CAVEAT/UNVERIFIED: on this Windows box realpath collapsed `..` through a missing intermediate, so I could NOT make realpath throw and could NOT execute the :533-534 fallback at runtime here. The branch's existence is proven by the source line; its reachability on POSIX (where realpath(2) requires every component to exist, so a client path with a missing intermediate yields ENOENT) is reasoned, not measured.

## [v2]

reason: REFUTED on portability. The claim is a faithful description of dsh's file (all six elements verified at line level), so it cannot be refuted on accuracy — but it would be a clear regression to port into omp.

1) The vocabulary does not exist. dsh's entire mechanism is spelled in Electron: `app.dock?.bounce`, `parent.flashFrame()`, `parent.isFocused()`, Electron `Notification`. omp is a Bun CLI/TUI with no Electron app shell — grep for `BrowserWindow|flashFrame|dock\.|isFocused()` across packages/ returns only browser-automation and packaging hits. (Correction to an earlier stale grep of mine: Electron does appear in omp, but only as an *external* CDP automation target via `tools/browser/attach.ts:448 pickElectronTarget`, ASAR reading in `utils/src/ar/asar.ts`, and xterm-on-Electron terminal comments. Never as omp's own window/app.)

2) The two focus mechanics are unimplementable, not merely unimplemented. `parent.isFocused()` (line 26) and `parent.on('focus', clear)` (lines 29-30) require owning an OS window. A terminal has none, and the only in-band mechanism a terminal could use to report it — xterm focus events, CSI ?1004 — is absent: grep for `?1004|focusIn|focusOut|windowFocus|terminalFocused` in packages/tui/src returns 0 hits. Every `focus` identifier in tui/src is internal widget focus (which row/pane the keyboard cursor sits on). Any substitute (e.g. inferring focus from recent keystrokes) is a fabricated heuristic that both suppresses reminders the user never saw and fires attention while they are watching.

5) omp already ships the better version of this exact surface. `main.ts:223-234` runs a gated startup version check, and `ui-helpers.ts:1074-1088 showNewVersionNotification` renders a bordered in-transcript banner pointing at `omp update`. 6) The headline invariant is already enforced by the type system, so the port is a no-op. The claim's most valuable element is "attention never grants authorization." reason: The mechanism is real and correctly described in dsh, but it is NOT portable to omp, and omp is already the stronger implementation. Four independent blockers, each measured in omp's own code:

(1) THE CLAIM'S DISTINCTIVE CLAUSE HAS NO TARGET IN omp. "Keyed by scope" requires per-scope identity. omp has exactly one MCP scope: the process. MCPManager is a process-global singleton (manager.ts:246-256, `static #instance` / `instance()` / `setInstance()`); sdk.ts:2354 installs it only for ROOT sessions (`if (mcpManager && !options.parentTaskPrefix)`), and subagents inherit rather than get their own (task/structured-subagent.ts:530: `session.mcpManager ?? MCPManager.instance()`). So "agent-scoped servers may reuse a namespace in another Agent" describes a capability omp structurally does not have. The WeakMap would key every instance to the same process-global owner, collapsing the exact distinction the claim is about — it would make agent-scoped reuse IMPOSSIBLE to express, not preserved. Porting requires first building per-agent MCP scoping: an architectural change, not a lift-and-shift.

(2) IT WOULD BREAK A DOCUMENTED, TESTED PRECEDENCE CONTRACT. omp's duplicate serverName is deliberate silent shadowing by source priority, not a config error: capability/index.ts:227 comment "Deduplicate by key or semantic equivalence (first wins = highest priority)"; :264-274 marks the loser `item._shadowed = true` and drops it with NO warning appended. mcpCapability.key is `server => server.name` (capability/mcp.ts:112). A hard-throw reservation keyed on the session would convert the ordinary "project `.mcp.json` overrides my user-level `foo`" case into a startup failure. That exact override is locked in by packages/coding-agent/test/mcp-config-scope-dedup.test.ts ("project server can shadow a differently-named ... user server"; "a disabled project `foo` keeps a same-named, lower-priority user `foo` disabled"), and config.ts:136-140 documents that a disabled entry must still own its name at key-level dedupe. Also note dsh has no equivalent axis: two entries in one cordis.yml are same-scope (error), whereas omp's collision axis is source PRIORITY (legitimate override). Mapping reservation→precedence inverts the semantics.

(3) omp ALREADY SOLVES THE HARDER, ADJACENT PROBLEM, AND dsh's reservation CANNOT TOUCH IT. dsh's reservation only prevents duplicate serverNames; it is structurally blind to tool-name mint collisions between DISTINCT serverNames. omp has to defend against exactly that: `deduplicateMCPToolsByName` (tool-bridge.ts:598-636) keeps one tool per minted name and picks the winner by a stable origin key (`server\u0000tool`), not array order — the comment at :591-597 explains why first-wins would silently flip ownership because MCPManager re-appends a reconnecting server's tools, and :626 `logger.warn`s the collision. It also dedups by connection equivalence (`equivalent: isSameMCPConnection`, mcp.ts:113), catching differently-named same-endpoint servers. dsh has no analogue for either, because its clean `mcp__<server>__<tool>` concatenation makes the collision impossible. Porting the reservation would add a weaker guard for an easier case while leaving omp's harder one untouched.

(4) omp ALREADY FAILS LOUD, ON THE RIGHT SIDE. config-writer.ts:131-134 throws `Server "${name}" already exists in ${filePath}"` on the WRITE path. Leniency is confined to the READ path, which is the correct split: overriding your own user-level config from a project file is legitimate and should not abort the session, whereas two writes racing to the same file is a genuine error.

RESIDUE WORTH BORROWING (narrow, and NOT the reservation): a shadowed MCP server is reported ONLY in the TUI dashboard — `_shadowed` is read at exactly one place, modes/components/extensions/state-manager.ts:183. There is no logger.warn on the config-level shadow path, in contrast to the tool-level collision at tool-bridge.ts:626. So a user whose project-level `foo` is shadowed by a user-level `foo` silently gets a different server than the one they wrote, with no console or log signal. Adding a `logger.warn` there is a real, small observability gap — but it is a one-line logging addition, not a load-time reservation/effect port.

TIER: DO-NOT-COPY the scope-keyed WeakMap reservation (breaks tested precedence, inapplicable axis). REFERENCE dsh's "reserve before side effects, release in the effect cleanup" ordering discipline (:162-176 before :181) as a readability pattern. BORROW only the shadow warning. omp is already better on this concern.

reason: REFUTED as stated, from both the provenance and the measurement axis. The claim has three separable parts: (a) "40-line entry", (b) "serving browser and embedded-Electron from one code path", (c) "which is what makes the whole UI testable in a zero-build source mode". (a) is TRUE and measured — apps/web/src/main.ts is exactly 40 lines (wc -l), 3 of which are a brand-font CSS import, and it is the sole script tag in apps/web/index.html:13. (b) is TRUE — the desktop main process serves the *identical built artifact* from node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-frontend/dist (apps/desktop/src/main.ts:640-642), and the entry branches on a single presence check, `globalThis.dshDesktopBoot` (main.ts:11), which is exposed by the Electron preload at apps/desktop/src/preload-app.ts:84; that global is absent in a browser tab, so one 40-line file genuinely serves both. (c) is FALSE, and it is the load-bearing part of the claim: the causal story is inverted. The web UI is NOT testable in a zero-build source mode. `test:web` in the root package.json is literally `npm run build && npm run test:web:built` — a full build is mandatory, and `test:web:built` is what actually runs. The 206-scenario snapshot harness confirms it from the other side: apps/web/tests/assembled-boot.ts:1-2 says it boots "the real built workspace `lib/client.js` artifacts" and it resolves those artifacts through packages/bundle/base and packages/bundle/web-app manifests, requiring each package's built `./client` export. I confirmed zero lib/ dirs exist in a clean checkout, so the suite cannot run unbuilt. Searching for the concept under every other plausible name (source mode / sourceMode / SOURCE_MODE / zero-build / zero-config / no-build / from-source / in-process-src / tsx-source) across apps/web, packages/client/web and vitest.web.config.ts returned 0 hits, so this is not a naming miss. The real testability lever is something else entirely: a `seams` / `loadBundle` transport injection point (boot.ts:19-20, `export type BootSeams = Pick<ClientModuleCreateOptions,'loadBundle'>`) that lets tests swap the module transport, plus the a11y-tree golden snapshots the parent report already praises. Thinness is not the enabler. Provenance: dsh is cleanly MIT (root LICENSE, "Copyright (c) 2026 DeepSeek"), remote is github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness, and `scripts/verify-dsh-package-licenses.ts:59-68` CI-enforces `"license": "MIT"` on every @deepseek-ai/dsh* workspace manifest — so the 40 lines themselves ARE legally copyable into an MIT project. But copying them buys nothing: the file is a 40-line shim whose two imports resolve to 504 lines across 9 files in packages/client/web, which in turn mounts packages/client/ui-renderer (23 files / 6,376 lines) inside a Cordis context, over a 294,185-line, 1,677-file packages/client tree. 40 lines of MIT code sitting on top of 294K lines is not a pattern you can lift. The one non-MIT landmine on the import path is line 2: the brand font is Montserrat under SIL OFL (packages/client/ui-theme/src/styles/brand-font.css:1, with Montserrat-OFL.txt shipped alongside the woff2 files) — copy the import and you inherit an OFL notice obligation for the binaries, not just the CSS. omo is irrelevant to this verdict: the claim is sourced entirely from dsh, and dsh is MIT. Tiering: BORROW the `BootSeams`/`loadBundle` transport-injection point (genuinely portable, ~5 lines, and the actual reason the UI is testable) and the a11y-tree golden approach; REFERENCE the main.ts shape itself as a readable example of capability-detection branching; DO-NOT-COPY the claim as written — "thin entry ⇒ zero-build testability" is backwards, and adopting it would mean shipping a 40-line entry and believing your UI is testable when the suite still needs a full build. UNVERIFIED: whether Electron and browser render byte-identically at runtime (I read the serving code, did not launch either); whether some untested lane builds UI from source (0 hits across the searched trees, but I did not exhaust all ~184 scripts).

## [v3]

reason: REFUTED on three independent grounds — though NOT on license terms. Verbatim copying of dsh's `publicToolName` (7 lines) IS legally clean: dsh's root LICENSE is MIT (Copyright (c) 2026 DeepSeek), there is no package-level LICENSE override under `packages/mcp/` (checked: `find packages/mcp -iname "LICENSE*"` = 0 hits), dsh's CONTRIBUTING.md contains no CLA, and omp is MIT (Zechner/Bölük/Stencil Labs) with no CLA requirement. The failure is provenance + redundancy + correctness.

(1) PROVENANCE — the idea is not DeepSeek's to license. dsh's own design note states the `mcp__<server>__<tool>` spelling "follows Claude Code and Codex" and cites 8 upstream projects. The commit that introduced it (af3152fefe) is titled "adopt mainstream server-qualified MCP tool naming" — an adoption, not an invention. So the prefix scheme is Anthropic/OpenAI prior art reaching omp through an intermediary. The only dsh-specific residue is 12-hex SHA-256 on lossy normalization, a generic identity-hash technique omp already uses with different parameters.

(2) REDUNDANT — omp already implements a stronger equivalent in-tree (capMCPToolNameLength with an 8-char base-36 Bun.hash suffix; getMCPToolOriginKey building the SAME NUL-joined `${serverName}\u0000${toolName}` identity tuple dsh hashes; deduplicateMCPToolsByName with an order-independent deterministic winner). Both halves of "omp's long/duplicate tool-name question" are already answered.

(3) "COMPLETE ANSWER" IS FALSE — dsh's headline invariant is the exact OPPOSITE of what omp requires. dsh can afford "never parse the public name" only because it deliberately chose the `__` spelling. omp cannot: it must also serve models primed on Claude Code's spelling, so it is structurally forced to parse the emitted public name back into (server, tool) and re-mint. Adopting dsh's invariant would delete the only mechanism omp has for a failure observed in real transcripts.

Additional concrete regressions if copied: (a) switching omp's `mcp__<server>_<tool>` single-underscore mint to dsh's `__` mint renames every MCP tool — and omp already carries scar tissue from exactly this rename, having built `createLegacyMCPToolName` solely to keep old user config keys working, with approval.ts using the legacy key as a FAIL-CLOSED fallback so a rename cannot silently unblock a restricted MCP server; a second rename would re-break every `tools.approval` key. (b) dsh THROWS on a duplicate public name (tools.ts:126-130), taking an entire server's tool list offline on a benign cross-identity collision; omp deliberately picks a winner and logs.

Also: the claim's stated source "dsh/mcp-lsp-tools" does not exist. Checked `ls packages/mcp/` (only `mcp-client`, `mcp-resources`) and repo-wide grep for "mcp-lsp-tools" excluding node_modules/.git (0 hits). dsh does have a separate `packages/lsp/`, which is likely the source of the mislabel. 237  projectContent(exec, result) {
238    const projection = projections.get(exec)
239    if (projection === undefined) return undefined
240    projections.delete(exec)
241    if (result.isError) return undefined
242    if (!isDeepStrictEqual(result.value, projection.fallback-check A: projection.value)) return undefined
243    if (!isDeepStrictEqual(result.content, projection.fallback)) return undefined
244    return projection.content
245  }

PreparedProjection is declared at tools.ts:174-182 with exactly three fields: value, fallback, content.

(b) "STRICT DEEP EQUALITY" CONFIRMED. isDeepStrictEqual is imported from node:util at tools.ts:16 — the strict variant (prototype/tag-aware, -0 vs +0, own enumerable props). It is used at BOTH guard sites, 242 and 243.

(c) "EQUALS BOTH THE STAGED VALUE AND THE STAGED FALLBACK" CONFIRMED. Line 242 compares result.value against projection.value; line 243 compares result.content against projection.fallback. The fallback is staged at tools.ts:308 as [{ type: 'text', text: extractText(content, rawName) }], which is exactly what output.render returns for this tool (tools.ts:261-264) — so line 243 verifies nobody replaced the renderer output in between.
