## [omp:typebox-gap]

**COUNTS:** 29 pi packages probed in /tmp/pi-ext-probe; 17 import bare `typebox`; 57 bare-`typebox` import statements (excl. node_modules); 6 files import `typebox/value`; 4 files import `typebox/compile`; 13 distinct `Type.*` builders used; 2 type-only symbols (Static, TSchema). omp: 1 remap point for typebox (legacy-pi-compat.ts:1151) + 1 onResolve filter (:873); 0 remaps for subpaths; 0 tests covering subpaths. Tree: @sinclair/typebox@0.34.52 present (devDep of 1 package), bare typebox absent. Probe packages affected: 3 hard-fail (peer-absent), 1 fail-open split-brain, 1 masked maxProperties, rest OK on the bare specifier.

**FINDINGS:**
- Real pi extensions import bare `typebox` v1.x — a DIFFERENT npm package from `@sinclair/typebox@0.34.x`. They are not interchangeable.
  ev: Measured: bare `typebox` import statements = 57 across /tmp/pi-ext-probe (excluding node_modules); 17 of 29 probed packages import it. Declared ranges: pi-todo & @juicesharp/rpiv-todo `"typebox": "^1.1.24"`, pi-mcp-adapter `"typebox": "1.3.3"`, pi-web-access `"1.3.27"`, bigpowers `"^1.3.7"`, @narumitw/pi-goal `"1.3.34"`, pi-lens `"^1.0.0"`. By contrast `@sinclair/typebox` appears in only 2 packages (pi-fff `"^0.34.41"`, pi-simplify `"^0.34.0"`, @tintinweb/pi-subagents `"^0.34.49"`). A pi extension states the distinction itself — /tmp/pi-ext-probe/pkgs/_tintinweb_pi-subagents/package/src/workflow/json-schema.ts:10-11: "**`typebox`, not `@sinclair/typebox`.** They are different packages and both are installed here."
  impact: Invalidates the framing that "typebox" is one thing. Any fix targeting @sinclair/typebox targets the wrong package for 17/29 of the ecosystem.
- The API surface pi extensions actually use is tiny: 13 `Type.*` builders plus 2 type-only symbols. No exotic surface.
  ev: Extracted from only the files that actually import typebox (excl. node_modules and .d.ts): Type.Optional 645, Type.String 442, Type.Object 143, Type.Boolean 88, Type.Number 67, Type.Unsafe 61, Type.Integer 55, Type.Array 54, Type.Literal 18, Type.Union 13, Type.Unknown 5, Type.Record 2, Type.Any 1; types `Static` (11) and `TSchema` (6). Subpaths: `Check`+`Errors` from `typebox/value` (4 files), `Compile` from `typebox/compile` (2 files). The 1485 Type.SEQUENCE / 748 Type.OID / 429 Type.OCTETSTRING counts in a naive repo-wide grep are ASN.1 noise from a node_modules .d.ts, not plugin usage.
  impact: The gap is not builder coverage — it is subpath coverage. Scoping effort to the 13 builders overstates the work.
- omp's legacy-typebox mask IS wired at the bare `typebox` specifier (drop-in for the root), and covers all 13 builders — but it is an internal facade with a DIFFERENT VALUE MODEL, not a re-export of typebox.
  ev: Empirical rewrite probe via `__rewriteLegacyExtensionSourceForTests`: `import { Type } from "typebox"` -> `file:///.../extensibility/legacy-typebox.ts` (REWRITTEN); `import { Type } from "@sinclair/typebox"` -> same shim (REWRITTEN). Wiring is at legacy-pi-compat.ts:1151 (`specifier === "typebox" || specifier === "@sinclair/typebox"`), the Bun onResolve filter at :873, and the compiled-binary virtual key at :41/:941. legacy-typebox.ts:12 does `export * from "@oh-my-pi/omptype/typebox"`. Runtime probe: omptype `Type` has all 13 required builders (YES on every one). BUT: `typeof Type.Object({a: Type.String()})` === "function", and `JSON.stringify` of it returns `undefined` — omptype schemas are callable runtime validators, NOT plain JSON Schema objects like typebox v1's.
  impact: The import resolves and the builders are all present, so a smoke test on `Type.*` alone passes and looks like a drop-in. It is not: the object flowing downstream is a different shape.
- omp does NOT remap `typebox/value` or `typebox/compile`. This is by design, and it is the actual gap.
  ev: Same rewrite probe: `import { Check, Errors } from "typebox/value"` -> NOT rewritten. `import { Compile } from "typebox/compile"` -> NOT rewritten. Cause: `TYPEBOX_SPECIFIER_FILTER = /^(?:@sinclair\/typebox|typebox)$/` at legacy-pi-compat.ts:873 is `$`-anchored so subpaths never match; :1151 uses exact string equality; and :870-872 states the intent outright — "Submodules such as `@sinclair/typebox/compiler` are intentionally not remapped". Unmatched specifiers fall through to `isBareExtensionDependencySpecifier` -> `resolveExtensionBareDependency` (:1158-1161, :1757), which resolves only from the extension's own on-disk node_modules. The existing test packages/coding-agent/test/extensibility/typebox-remap.test.ts covers only the bare specifier (4 cases); no test covers either subpath.
  impact: This is the whole typebox gap, and it is untested. A package importing `typebox/value` is not covered by any regression test in the repo.
- Because typebox is an OPTIONAL PEER dependency in most pi packages, the common failure is a hard load error, not a subtle one.
  ev: Dependency kind measured: pi-subagents `peerDependencies {"typebox":"*"}` + `peerDependenciesMeta {"typebox":{"optional":true}}`; pi-mcp-adapter same (typebox only in devDeps); pi-web-access `peerDependencies {"typebox":"*"}`, typebox only in devDeps; pi-dynamic-workflows same. Only pi-todo has it as a hard `dependencies {"typebox":"^1.1.24"}`. Consequence: `bun install` in the plugins dir will NOT materialize typebox for the peer case, and a fresh import of `typebox/value` fails with "Cannot find package 'typebox'" (reproduced directly in probe2). 3 of 19 packages probed are in this state: pi-subagents, pi-mcp-adapter, @tintinweb/pi-subagents.
  impact: Loud failure, at least — the extension refuses to load rather than misbehaving quietly. But it still means those 3 packages are simply not runnable in omp today.
- When typebox IS installed, the result is worse than a crash: typebox v1's `Check` returns `true` for every input against an omp-produced schema. This is a silent fail-open.
  ev: Installed real typebox@1.3.27 and ran the cross-check. Against an omptype schema (`Type.Object({a: Type.String()})`, typeof "function"): Check -> true for {a:'hi'} (valid), {a:123}, {}, {a:'hi',b:9}, and 'nope' (all INVALID). Errors() -> [] in every case. Compile(schema).Check(value) -> true in every case, including 'nope'. Control against the same schema's `toJsonSchema()` wire JSON correctly returns false for 3 of the 4 invalid inputs. A pi extension that gets `Type` from omp's shim and `Check`/`Compile` from real typebox v1 therefore validates nothing, silently.
  impact: Security-relevant fail-open, not a UX bug. Anything a pi extension gates on schema validation (pi-subagents validates model-supplied structured output this way) accepts garbage. The fail is silent — no throw, no warning — so it would not surface in any smoke test.
- The same value-model mismatch applies to @sinclair/typebox packages: omp merges two deliberately-separate packages into one shim.
  ev: @tintinweb/pi-subagents declares BOTH `@sinclair/typebox ^0.34.49` and `typebox ^1.3.7`, and imports `@sinclair/typebox` in 10 files plus `typebox/value` in 2. omp rewrites the `@sinclair/typebox` root to the omptype shim (so its 0.34 JSON-Schema-object builders become callable omptype schemas) while `typebox/value` falls through to real v1 — producing the identical universal-accept. The comment at that package's json-schema.ts:10-11 documents the two-package split as intentional.
  impact: omp's blanket remap of the `@sinclair/typebox` root actively defeats a separation the ecosystem author relied on. Merging the two is the bug, not the fix.
- @sinclair/typebox@0.34.52 IS in the tree — but it is a devDependency of one package only, and it cannot substitute for `typebox` v1.
  ev: bun.lock:898 `"@sinclair/typebox": ["@sinclair/typebox@0.34.52", ...]`, declared at bun.lock:216 as `"@sinclair/typebox": "^0.34.0"`; sole declaration is packages/omptype/package.json:38 under **devDependencies**. node_modules/@sinclair/typebox/package.json confirms version 0.34.52. Bare `typebox` is absent: no `typebox` key in root package.json, no node_modules/typebox, no such bun.lock entry. Runtime probe of 0.34.52: it HAS all 13 `Type.*` builders. But its `value` subpath exports `Delete, Edit, Insert, Update, Value, ValueErrorType, ValuePointer, ValuePointerRootDeleteError, ValuePointerRootSetError, default` — i.e. `Value.Check`/`Value.Errors`, NOT the free functions `Check`/`Errors` that plugins import. And there is NO `compile` subpath: `import("@sinclair/typebox/compile")` fails with "Cannot find package '@sinclair/typebox'".
  impact: Confirms the M1B plan's claim that 0.34 is "API-incompatible" is directionally right but mis-diagnosed: the incompatibility is the subpath surface (no `Check`/`Errors` free exports, no `compile` subpath), not the builders — those are all present. Aliasing bare `typebox` to 0.34 would leave both subpaths still broken.
- Cheapest robust fix is a re-export shim, not a dependency: omptype can express Check, Errors and Compile in roughly one line each.
  ev: Verified against real omptype: `Check(S,v)` ~ `!(S(v) instanceof type.errors)`; `Errors(S,v)` ~ `S(v) instanceof type.errors ? S(v).map(e=>e.message) : []` (errors carry a usable path+message: `{"path":["a"],"message":"a must be a string (was a number)"}`); `Compile(S)` ~ `{ Check: v => !(S(v) instanceof type.errors) }` — omptype already JIT-compiles, so Compile is a wrapper, not a compiler. Cost: widen `TYPEBOX_SPECIFIER_FILTER` (legacy-pi-compat.ts:873) to `^typebox(/.*)?$`, add the matching branch at :1151, and export Check/Errors/Compile from legacy-typebox.ts (which already re-exports the omptype facade at :12). This needs no new npm dependency and keeps one schema engine.
  impact: Resolves the M1B blocker at near-zero cost and simultaneously fixes the ecosystem fail-open, because everything then comes from one engine. Adding real `typebox@1.3.x` as a dependency would NOT fix it — it preserves the omptype/v1 value-model split that causes the universal-accept.
- Layer (c) INSTALLABLE is real: omp has a working install path that runs a real `bun install`.
  ev: `omp plugin` is registered at packages/coding-agent/src/cli-commands.ts:169 (aliases `plugins`); installer.ts:47-48 runs `Bun.spawn(["bun","install",packageName], {cwd: PLUGINS_DIR})` where PLUGINS_DIR = `~/.omp/plugins` (installer.ts:6). So installing a third-party package works and materializes its real dependencies — which, per the optional-peer finding, deliberately does not include typebox.
  impact: Install is not the blocker. The blocker is strictly the specifier remap surface.
- Layer (a) BUNDLED does not apply to typebox at all — typebox was never pi's own source, so M1 vendoring could never have covered it.
  ev: typebox is a third-party npm package (typebox 1.3.27, repo github.com/sinclairzx81/typebox), never a `@earendil-works/pi-*` package. The bundled-surface files in extensibility/ are all shims over pi's own packages (legacy-pi-coding-agent-shim.ts 61KB, legacy-pi-ai-shim.ts, legacy-pi-tui-shim.ts) plus legacy-typebox.ts (179 lines) — which is a facade over omp's own @oh-my-pi/omptype, not vendored typebox.
  impact: Directly addresses the hypothesis under test: bundled capability here is a hand-written 179-line facade, so "M1 bundled pi so the pi ecosystem works" does not and cannot transfer to typebox.
- Residual builder-surface gap: `maxProperties` is silently dropped by the omptype mask, turning a validation constraint into a no-op.
  ev: Option-modifier scan across plugin files: description 321, default 59, minimum 48, enum 42, maxLength 34, minLength 30, maximum 14, additionalProperties 12, maxProperties 4, if/exclusiveMinimum/anyOf 4 each, pattern/then/not/else 2-3. In packages/omptype/src/typebox.ts, 13 of these 14 keys appear; `maxProperties` has 0 occurrences. Runtime test: `Type.Object({a,b},{maxProperties:1}).toJsonSchema()` emits `{"type":"object","properties":{...},"required":[...]}` with the keyword gone, and validating `{a:'x',b:'y'}` -> ACCEPTED. Contrast @sinclair/typebox 0.34.52: emits `{"maxProperties":1,...}` and Value.Check -> false.
  impact: Silent constraint loss at 4 ecosystem use sites — a second fail-open, independent of the subpath issue, and it survives even after the subpaths are fixed.
- Legal risk is nil: typebox is MIT and every probed pi package is MIT or ISC.
  ev: `npm`-installed typebox@1.3.27 package.json: `license: MIT`, repo github.com/sinclairzx81/typebox. Probed pi packages: pi-subagents MIT, pi-mcp-adapter MIT, pi-todo MIT, pi-web-access MIT, pi-dynamic-workflows MIT, @tintinweb/pi-subagents MIT, @juicesharp/rpiv-todo MIT, pi-background-tasks ISC.
  impact: No licensing obstacle to either shipping real typebox or reimplementing the surface on omptype.
- The M1B blocker as written is a different question from the ecosystem question, and its factual premises check out.
  ev: MILESTONE_1_EXECUTION_PLAN.md (Phần B):40-42 states typebox is "chưa chốt", that omp has no typebox in the lockfile, only `@sinclair/typebox@0.34.52` — "dependency transitive, khác API" — and no `node_modules/typebox`. All three verified true (bun.lock:898 is the sole typebox-family entry; it is a devDependency of omptype, not even a runtime transitive). But M1B's decision is "when we copy pi-protocol INTO omp, which engine do we author against" — an in-repo rewrite choice. The ecosystem question is "does a third-party extension that imports typebox run", which is answered above and is not answered by M1B's recommendation.
  impact: The plan recommends porting pi-protocol to omptype. That recommendation is sound for its own question and was independently re-verified here (all builders present, only `Check` missing, 1-line `instanceof type.errors` idiom available). It must not be read as resolving the ecosystem subpath gap.

**UNVERIFIED:**
- Could not execute the repo's own typebox-remap test or loadLegacyPiModule end-to-end: packages/natives has no built pi_natives addon on this machine (`pi_natives.win32-x64{,-modern,-baseline}.node` all absent), and every path into legacy-typebox.ts transitively loads it via @oh-my-pi/pi-utils/dirs. The rewrite-layer conclusions come from `__rewriteLegacyExtensionSourceForTests` (which does run) plus the isolated omptype/typebox@0.34.52/typebox@1.3.27 runtime probes (which do run), not from a full extension load.
- Whether omp's plugin loader surfaces the `typebox/value` failure as a clean per-extension error or a hard process crash was not determined — that requires loading a real extension, which the natives gap blocks.
- Whether pi's own host ships a real `typebox@1.3.x` inside the installed pi package (pi-subagents' runner-aliases.js implies the host must, since it aliases `typebox`, `typebox/compile` and `typebox/value` to package `typebox`) was not verified against a pi installation — only against the extracted extension tarballs, which are third-party packages and do not contain the host copy.
- The probe corpus is 29 packages, not the full pi.dev registry. The 3-package split-brain and 4-package hard-fail counts are lower bounds for the probed set; the true ecosystem rate is unmeasured.
- Whether `Type.Enum`, `Type.Null` or other omptype builders that no probed extension used would satisfy untested usage is unknown; the coverage claim is limited to the 13 builders actually observed.



## [omp:legacy-pi-compat]

**COUNTS:** 1 file read in full (2784 lines) + 2 loaders + 4 manifests + 4 pi package.json files. 3 controlled Bun experiments (onResolve-only, onLoad-rewrite, statically-linked-importer). 1 faithful replication of remapLegacyPiSpecifier + resolveCanonicalPiSpecifier over 20 real specifiers. 56 runtime pi-coding-agent imports diffed against the omp source tree. 4 manifests license-checked. 15 findings, 6 unverified items. No repo files modified (git status shows only pre-existing changes from other agents in the shared worktree).

**FINDINGS:**
- It is NOT plugin/extension ID normalization and NOT a runtime import map. It is (ii)+(iii): a Babel-AST source-TEXT rewrite that pre-substitutes import/require specifiers with absolute `file://` URLs (or `omp-legacy-pi-bundled:<key>` virtual specifiers in compiled mode) BEFORE Bun ever resolves them. The rewrite splices string literals back into the source using recorded character offsets.
  ev: legacy-pi-compat.ts:63-91 `parseExtensionSource` uses `@babel/parser`; :461-536 `collectExtensionSpecifierReferences` walks the AST with real lexical-scope tracking (shadowed `require`/`exports`/`module` excluded, :423-429, :416-421) and returns `{kind, specifier, start, end}`; :721-730 `applySpecifierReplacements` does `${rewritten.slice(0,start)}${JSON.stringify(replacement)}${rewritten.slice(end)}`. No resolver is consulted at import time — the text is already canonical.
  impact: Correct mental model: 'import-map style module resolution' is closest, but it is eager and textual, not lazy and resolver-based. Consequence: any specifier form the Babel walk misses (computed/dynamic template specifiers, `eval`, worker-constructed specifiers) is never rewritten and fails hard at import time.
- It rewrites FIVE distinct specifier classes in a third-party extension's own source, plus a separate CommonJS pass.
  ev: legacy-pi-compat.ts:1142-1150 legacy `@(scope)/pi-*` -> `@oh-my-pi/...`; :1151-1153 bare `typebox`/`@sinclair/typebox` -> omptype facade; :1154-1157 package `imports` aliases (`#src/*`); :1158-1161 extension-local bare deps via the extension's own node_modules; :1162-1164 relative `./`/`../` get a `?mtime=` cache-bust. Separately :1902-1934 `collectExtensionSpecifierReplacements` rewrites bare `require()` targets, backed by a synchronous CJS bridge registered on `globalThis.__ompLegacyPiRequireGraphModule` (:2000, :2091-2097).
  impact: Scope is broad — this is a real general-purpose extension module loader, not a narrow scope alias. It is a much stronger asset than a name-mapping table, and it does solve (b) RESOLVABLE for a meaningful subset.
- ANSWER to 'does it run for a third-party extension that writes `import { X } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent"` in its OWN source file': YES, but only via exactly one call path, and only for the `extensions` manifest surface.
  ev: Call path: extensions/loader.ts:59 `installLegacyPiSpecifierShim()` -> :572-661 `discoverExtensionPaths` -> :485-488 `loadExtensions` -> :416-436 `importExtensionModule` -> legacy-pi-compat.ts:2613 `loadLegacyPiModule` -> :2618-2620 realpath + `ensureExtensionGraphHook` -> :2527 `ensureExtensionGraphHook` -> :2141 `collectExtensionModules` (static graph walk from the entry) -> :2412 `installExtensionGraphHook` registers a per-extension `Bun.plugin` onLoad over the exact realpaths -> :1126 `rewriteLegacyExtensionSource`. `grep -rn 'loadLegacyPiModule' packages/ --include='*.ts'` returns exactly ONE production call site (extensions/loader.ts:419); all other hits are tests.
  impact: The rewrite is real and reaches extension source. But the single call site is a fragility: any new plugin surface that imports modules must remember to route through loadLegacyPiModule or it silently loses pi compatibility.
- MEASURED: the `onResolve` half of this file is DEAD at runtime on this host. The shim only works via the `onLoad` source-rewrite path.
  ev: Control experiment `/tmp/pi-probe/control.ts` (fresh graph, onResolve only, filter `^@legacy-scope\/.*`, namespace 'file'): `IMPORT FAILED: Cannot find package '@legacy-scope/pi-y' imported from .../ext3/index.ts` and `onResolve hits: 0 []`. Second control `/tmp/pi-probe/hostctrl.ts` (statically-linked importer instead of runtime-imported): also 0 onResolve hits. Paired experiment `/tmp/pi-probe/full2.ts` (same graph, onLoad filter `\.ts$`): `hook hits: [onLoad .../index.ts, onLoad .../helper.ts, onLoad .../dep.ts]` and the bare specifier DID resolve after text substitution (it then failed only on my fixture's missing named export). Environment: `bun --version` = 1.4.2, Windows x64.
  impact: MAJOR. `installLegacyPiSpecifierShim()` (:2727-2778) registers onResolve for LEGACY_PI_SPECIFIER_FILTER (:2736), TYPEBOX_SPECIFIER_FILTER (:2737), and the three bundled virtual schemes (:2738-2752) — none of which intercept an extension's imports. The file's own header comment (:24-28) already warned that 'Bun.plugin onResolve also no longer fires for transitive imports inside runtime-loaded extensions'; I measured that on 1.4.2 it also does not fire for the ENTRY's own imports, and not for statically linked importers either. The repo's own reasoning at :2674-2679 (that onResolve 'still' helps host code) is not what makes extensions work.
- Two plugin manifest surfaces bypass the shim completely — an `omp`/`pi` plugin shipping a `commands` or `tools` entry that imports `@earendil-works/pi-*` has NO rewrite path.
  ev: packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/custom-commands/loader.ts:41 `const module = await import(commandPath);` and packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/custom-tools/loader.ts:78 `const module = await withHostGuard(() => import(resolvedPath));`. Both are raw dynamic imports with no `collectExtensionModules` walk, no per-path onLoad hook, and no `loadLegacyPiModule`. Reachable from real plugins via plugins/loader.ts:394-402 (`getAllPluginCommandPaths`) and :394-396 (`getAllPluginToolPaths`), consumed at custom-tools/loader.ts:266.
  impact: Direct counterexample to 'M1 made omp a strict superset of pi' at the extension surface: the same package.json that works under `pi: { extensions: [...] }` breaks under `pi: { commands: [...] }` or `pi: { tools: [...] }` if it imports a pi host package. Measured but unquantified for the 4 sampled pi packages — none of them shipped `commands`/`tools` manifest entries, so this may be latent rather than currently hit.
- CANONICAL_PI_SCOPE / PI_SCOPE_ALIASES / PI_PACKAGE_NAMES / LEGACY_PI_SPECIFIER_FILTER are all third-party-loading policy. NONE of them affects omp internal naming — nothing in omp renames its own modules through this file.
  ev: CANONICAL_PI_SCOPE (:796, not exported) = the single scope every legacy specifier is rewritten INTO. PI_SCOPE_ALIASES (:802) = the ACCEPTED SOURCE scopes; `@oh-my-pi` is deliberately included (comment :798-801) so canonical self-imports also take the host path instead of a plugin-local copy. PI_PACKAGE_NAMES (:805) = the 6 basenames the canonicaliser serves — an axis INDEPENDENT of scope, not derived from it. LEGACY_PI_SPECIFIER_FILTER (:837) = the composed regex, used both as the fast gate inside `remapLegacyPiSpecifier` (:1058, hit by every rewrite path) and as the onResolve filter at :2736.
  impact: Answering the plan's implicit question directly: all four are load-time policy for FOREIGN code. Editing them can only change what a third-party extension's import resolves to — which is exactly why M5's W2b (`CANONICAL_PI_SCOPE = '@ultraworkers'`) is a breaking change for every installed pi package.
- PI_PACKAGE_NAMES (6) covers only a third of the scoped packages omp publishes (16). The other 10 are never canonicalised.
  ev: legacy-pi-compat.ts:805 lists exactly `pi-agent-core, pi-ai, pi-coding-agent, pi-natives, pi-tui, pi-utils`. Repo-wide: `grep -m1 '"name"' packages/*/package.json` yields 16 scoped packages; the uncovered ones include `pi-catalog`, `omptype`, `pi-metaharness`, `pi-mnemopi`, `pi-wire`, `omp-stats`, `snapcompact`, `browser-relay`, `collab-web`, `typescript-edit-benchmark`. Simulation confirms `@ultraworkers/omp-stats` does not match the filter.
  impact: Any pi extension that reaches for a pi package outside these 6 gets no host routing at all and must ship its own copy — which reintroduces exactly the duplicate-native-module hazard the shim exists to prevent. Matches M5's W2-6 note.
- LAYER (b) RESOLVABLE — measured coverage. All 6 pi package ROOTS resolve; `pi-ai/oauth`, `pi-ai/utils/oauth`, and `pi-ai/compat` resolve. Three real pi subpaths do NOT.
  ev: Replication of `remapLegacyPiSpecifier` + `resolveCanonicalPiSpecifier` (`/tmp/pi-probe/resolve.ts`, verbatim constants from :796-837, :1057-1096): roots resolve via override table to `packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/legacy-{pi-ai,pi-coding-agent,pi-tui}-shim.ts` (all three confirmed on disk), or via `Bun.resolveSync` to packages/{ai,agent,tui,utils,coding-agent}/src/index.ts and packages/natives/native/index.js. `pi-ai/oauth` and `pi-ai/utils/oauth` -> packages/ai/src/registry/oauth/index.ts. FAILS: `@earendil-works/pi-ai/providers/all`, `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core/node`, `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/<any-subpath-not-in-our-exports>` — all three named in real pi manifests at /tmp/pi-ext-probe/pi-subagents-0.73.1/package/src/runs/background/runner-aliases.js:19,24 and :22. Underlying cause: `packages/ai/src/providers/all.ts` and `packages/agent/src/node.ts` do not exist, though the exports patterns `./*` and `./providers/*` match them.
  impact: The (b) layer is substantially real but not closed. The gap is subpath-level, which is exactly the surface real pi packages advertise.
- `@earendil-works/chord` and `@earendil-works/chord/context` are not remapped at all — the shim never sees them.
  ev: PI_PACKAGE_NAMES (:805) has no `chord`, so LEGACY_PI_SPECIFIER_FILTER (:837) does not match. `/tmp/pi-probe/resolve.ts` prints `NO-REMAP @earendil-works/chord` and `NO-REMAP @earendil-works/chord/context`. pi-subagents' own source documents this as a live upstream surface: runner-aliases.js:29 `/** Public Pi manifests introduce chord in 0.85.0 (absent through 0.84.4). */` with the two CHORD_PEER_ALIASES entries at :31-32.
  impact: A whole upstream peer package is invisible to the canonicaliser. Any extension importing chord falls through to Bun's native node_modules walk from the extension dir, where the (optional) peer is not installed -> unresolvable at load. Mitigating: in the 4 sampled packages chord appears only in the alias table, never as a direct import.
- TypeBox subpath specifiers are not remapped — the filter is anchored.
  ev: legacy-pi-compat.ts:873 `const TYPEBOX_SPECIFIER_FILTER = /^(?:@sinclair\/typebox|typebox)$/;` and the rewrite gate at :1151 `specifier === "typebox" || specifier === "@sinclair/typebox"`. Real pi packages import `typebox/compile` and `typebox/value` (pi-subagents-0.73.1/package/src/runs/background/binary-bootstrap.js:7-8; runner-aliases.js:26-28). The comment at :869-872 says this is intentional, but the 4 sampled packages do import those subpaths.
  impact: Deliberate design, correctly documented, but it means a TypeBox-flavoured extension gets a SPLIT runtime: bare `typebox` goes to the omptype facade, `typebox/compile` goes to whatever the extension's own node_modules has. Two TypeBox instances in one process.
- The next wall after resolution is API-surface: two runtime symbols real pi extensions import do not exist anywhere in omp, and two more exist but are not re-exported through the pi-ai compat route.
  ev: `withFileMutationQueue` — 0 hits in `packages/` (`grep -rn 'withFileMutationQueue' packages/`); imported as a VALUE by /tmp/pi-ext-probe/pi-mcp-adapter-3.1.0/package/index.ts:1 and CALLED at :1762. `ModelRuntime` — called as `pi.ModelRuntime.create()` at pi-subagents-0.73.1/package/src/runs/shared/child-session.js:205,215; only unrelated internal names exist in omp (config/model-discovery.ts:215,677,755). `complete` and `getEnvApiKey` are defined at packages/ai/src/stream.ts:1133 and :855 but are NOT in the pi-ai barrel nor in legacy-pi-ai-shim.ts (which is `export * from "@oh-my-pi/pi-ai"` at :133 plus explicit re-exports at :143,193,194); pi-memory calls `complete(...)` at pkgs/pi-memory/package/index.ts:467 via `@earendil-works/pi-ai/compat`, and _companion-ai_feynman imports `getEnvApiKey` at pkgs/_companion-ai_feynman/package/dist/model/catalog.js:2. `MarkdownOptions` (pi-tui) is absent too — type-only, so it breaks `bun check` on the extension, not runtime.
  impact: Resolving the specifier is necessary but NOT sufficient. Even a perfectly-remapped extension dies on Bun's static named-export check. This is the layer where 'bundled superset' is provably false today, and it is invisible to any test that only asserts specifier resolution.
- M5's documented failure mode #1 (dev mode: canonicaliser dies silently because the resolve error is swallowed by try/catch) — VERIFIED, with zero diagnostics.
  ev: legacy-pi-compat.ts:1142-1150, read verbatim from source: `const remappedSpecifier = remapLegacyPiSpecifier(specifier); if (remappedSpecifier) { try { replacement = toImportSpecifier(resolveCanonicalPiSpecifier(remappedSpecifier)); } catch { /* Compiled fallback may be absent from a malformed build. ... */ } }` — a bare `catch {}` containing only a comment and NO `logger` call at any level. `getResolvedSpecifier` (:1071-1080) is just `Bun.resolveSync(specifier, import.meta.dir)` and throws for an unknown scope. `replacement` stays null, control falls to the bare-dependency branch (:1158-1161) which operates on the ORIGINAL specifier, and if that also misses the specifier is left untouched.
  impact: CONFIRMED, and stronger than the plan states: it is not merely unlogged, it is unlogged at every level including `logger.debug`, while the surrounding file uses `logger.debug` liberally elsewhere (:607, :668, :694). Any scope/registry mismatch is invisible until the extension fails at import time with Bun's own error.
- M5's documented failure mode #2 (compiled binary: hard crash on every bundled extension load) — VERIFIED as a code path, not executed.
  ev: legacy-pi-compat.ts:750-758: `const loaders = await ensureBundledModuleLoadersLoaded(); const loader = loaders[moduleKey]; if (!loader) { throw new Error(\`omp:legacy-pi-shim: no bundled module registered for ${moduleKey}\`); }`. Reached from the BUNDLED_VIRTUAL_NAMESPACE onLoad (:2757-2758), from `resolveExtensionCommonJsRequire` (:1880-1883), and from the graph walk. Registry keys are the literal manifest names: packages/coding-agent/scripts/legacy-pi-virtual-module.ts:126 `addEntry(manifest.name, ...)`. So flipping CANONICAL_PI_SCOPE to `@ultraworkers` while manifests still say `@oh-my-pi` produces virtual specifiers with no registered key.
  impact: M5's claim is accurate. Note the asymmetry the plan understates: dev fails SILENTLY (recoverable-looking, plugin might load via a duplicate) while compiled fails LOUDLY. The loud one is the safer one; the silent one is the actual hazard.
- LAYER (c) INSTALLABLE — this file does not install anything, and omp has no pi.dev package index.
  ev: legacy-pi-compat.ts contains zero network/install code (2784 lines read in full). Installation lives elsewhere: extensibility/plugins/installer.ts:48 `Bun.spawn(["bun","install", packageName])`, :95 uninstall, manager.ts:538 and :1154 same pattern. `grep -rn 'pi\.dev' packages/ --include='*.ts'` returns 0 hits. `grep -rn 'installLegacyPiSpecifierShim' packages/coding-agent/scripts/ scripts/` returns 0 hits — the shim is never used at build time either.
  impact: Layer (c) is npm-name-based only. A user must already know the npm package name; pi.dev acts purely as a discovery website. Nothing in omp reads or mirrors a pi.dev index, so 'install everything from pi.dev' has no mechanism behind it at all.
- Discovery of an ALREADY-INSTALLED pi package does work: omp accepts a `pi` manifest key as an alternative to `omp`.
  ev: packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/plugins/loader.ts:179 `const manifest: PluginManifest | undefined = pluginPkg.omp || pluginPkg.pi;` then :180-183 skips only if neither exists. Confirmed against the 4 sampled manifests, which declare only `pi` (pi-todo-1.2.0 `pi.extensions: ["./src/index.ts"]`, @juicesharp/rpiv-todo `pi.extensions: ["./index.ts"]`).
  impact: The manifest-compatibility half of the ecosystem story is genuinely closed. The break is downstream, at module resolution and API surface — not at discovery.
- Even a perfectly-loaded parent extension can escape the shim: pi-subagents spawns a detached Node child and resolves pi host packages there against an INSTALLED pi package root, which omp does not have.
  ev: /tmp/pi-ext-probe/pi-subagents-0.73.1/package/src/runs/background/async-execution.js:4 `import { spawn } from "node:child_process"`, :22-23 imports pi-spawn and runner-aliases, :475 `[JITI_ALIAS_ENV]: binaryHost ? undefined : JSON.stringify(hostPeerAliases.aliases)`, :483 `const proc = spawn(command, args, ...)`. runner-aliases.js:1-13 states the design: 'pi's own extension loader aliases those specifiers to the copies shipped inside the installed pi package; the parent computes the same map and hands it to the runner through JITI_ALIAS'.
  impact: `Bun.plugin` is process-local — a spawned child inherits nothing. This is a structural limit of the shim's design (in-process, Bun-only) that no amount of specifier rewriting fixes. Any pi extension that delegates work to a subprocess is outside the compat layer entirely.
- Legal: all 4 sampled real pi packages are MIT.
  ev: `license` field read from each extracted manifest: pi-todo-1.2.0 = "MIT", @juicesharp/rpiv-todo 2.11.0 = "MIT", pi-mcp-adapter 3.1.0 = "MIT", pi-subagents 0.73.1 = "MIT".
  impact: No legal blocker in the sample. This does NOT generalise to the whole pi.dev catalogue, which was not enumerated.
- VERDICT on the hypothesis under test ('M1 already made omp a strict superset of pi, therefore omp can run the pi.dev package ecosystem'): the hypothesis is FALSE as stated, but the mechanism is real and better than the plans assume.
  ev: Supporting (a)+(b) partially: 6/6 package roots resolve, 3 shims exist on disk (1658/194/43/179 lines), `pi` manifests are discovered. Refuting (b): 3 advertised subpaths unresolvable, `chord` invisible to the filter, 2 runtime symbols absent repo-wide, 2 more unexported through the compat route. Refuting (c): 0 references to pi.dev anywhere in packages/. Additional refutations outside this file: custom-commands/loader.ts:41 and custom-tools/loader.ts:78 bypass the shim entirely; the shim is process-local so subprocess-delegating extensions escape it.
  impact: The plan's optimism comes from conflating (a) with (b) and (c), exactly as hypothesised. But the correction is NOT 'the shim does not work' — it demonstrably works for the extensions surface. The real gaps are (i) an API-surface delta (2 symbols entirely missing, 2 unexported), (ii) 3 subpaths + 1 whole package (`chord`) outside the filter, (iii) 2 of 3 plugin manifest surfaces not routed through the loader, and (iv) no pi.dev index and no subprocess story. Those are four separable work items, not one rewrite.
